preamble.title: Purpose of the Constitution
preamble.plain: The People of the State of California, grateful to Almighty God for their freedom, establish this Constitution to secure and perpetuate its blessings.

a1-s1.title: Inalienable rights
a1-s1.plain: All people are by nature free and independent and have inalienable rights, among them enjoying and defending life and liberty, acquiring, possessing, and protecting property, and pursuing and obtaining safety, happiness, and privacy.
rights: inalienable rights
enjoying and defending life and liberty
acquiring, possessing, and protecting property
pursuing and obtaining safety, happiness, and privacy

a1-s1.1.title: Reproductive freedom
a1-s1.1.plain: The state shall not deny or interfere with an individual's reproductive freedom in their most intimate decisions, including the fundamental right to choose to have an abortion and to choose or refuse contraceptives.
rights: reproductive freedom in their most intimate decisions
fundamental right to choose to have an abortion
fundamental right to choose or refuse contraceptives
limits: The state shall not deny or interfere with

a1-s2.title: Freedom of speech and press; news sources
a1-s2.plain: Every person may freely speak, write and publish on all subjects, being responsible for abuse of this right, and no law may restrain speech or press. News reporters and others may not be held in contempt for refusing to disclose sources or unpublished information.
rights: freely speak, write and publish his or her sentiments on all subjects
limits: A law may not restrain or abridge liberty of speech or press
shall not be adjudged in contempt
be so adjudged in contempt

a1-s3.title: Petition, assembly and public access to information
a1-s3.plain: The people have the right to instruct their representatives, petition government, and assemble freely, and the right of access to information about the people's business; meetings of public bodies and writings of public officials and agencies shall be open to public scrutiny.
rights: to instruct their representatives
petition government for redress of grievances
assemble freely to consult for the common good
the right of access to information concerning the conduct of the people’s business
limits: shall be adopted with findings demonstrating the interest protected by the limitation and the need for protecting that interest

a1-s4.title: Freedom of religion
a1-s4.plain: Free exercise and enjoyment of religion without discrimination or preference are guaranteed, but this does not excuse licentious acts or acts inconsistent with the State's peace or safety. The Legislature shall make no law respecting an establishment of religion.
rights: Free exercise and enjoyment of religion without discrimination or preference are guaranteed
limits: The Legislature shall make no law respecting an establishment of religion
A person is not incompetent to be a witness or juror because of his or her opinions on religious beliefs

a1-s5.title: Military subordinate to civil power
a1-s5.plain: The military is subordinate to civil power. No standing army may be kept in peacetime, and soldiers may not be quartered in any house in wartime except as prescribed by law, or in peacetime without the owner's consent.
limits: A standing army may not be maintained in peacetime
Soldiers may not be quartered in any house

a1-s6.title: Slavery and involuntary servitude prohibited
a1-s6.plain: Slavery is prohibited. Involuntary servitude is prohibited except to punish crime.
limits: Slavery is prohibited
Involuntary servitude is prohibited

a1-s7.title: Due process, equal protection and privileges
a1-s7.plain: A person may not be deprived of life, liberty, or property without due process of law or denied equal protection of the laws. It limits obligations about pupil school assignment or transportation, and bars privileges or immunities not granted on the same terms to all citizens.
rights: A person may not be deprived of life, liberty, or property without due process of law or denied equal protection of the laws
powers: Privileges or immunities granted by the Legislature may be altered or revoked
limits: no court of this State may impose upon the State of California or any public entity, board, or official any obligation or responsibility with respect to the use of pupil school assignment or pupil transportation
may not be granted privileges or immunities not granted on the same terms to all citizens

a1-s7.5.title: Right to marry
a1-s7.5.plain: The right to marry is a fundamental right. This section furthers the inalienable rights guaranteed by Section 1 and the rights to due process and equal protection guaranteed by Section 7.
rights: The right to marry is a fundamental right

a1-s8.title: No job disqualification for sex, race, creed
a1-s8.plain: A person may not be disqualified from entering or pursuing a business, profession, vocation, or employment because of sex, race, creed, color, or national or ethnic origin.
limits: may not be disqualified from entering or pursuing a business, profession, vocation, or employment

a1-s9.title: No bills of attainder or ex post facto laws
a1-s9.plain: A bill of attainder, an ex post facto law, or a law impairing the obligation of contracts may not be passed.
limits: A bill of attainder, ex post facto law, or law impairing the obligation of contracts may not be passed

a1-s10.title: Witness detention and imprisonment for debt
a1-s10.plain: Witnesses may not be unreasonably detained. A person may not be imprisoned in a civil action for debt or tort, or in peacetime for a militia fine.
limits: Witnesses may not be unreasonably detained
may not be imprisoned in a civil action for debt or tort, or in peacetime for a militia fine

a1-s11.title: Habeas corpus
a1-s11.plain: Habeas corpus may not be suspended unless required by public safety in cases of rebellion or invasion.
limits: Habeas corpus may not be suspended

a1-s12.title: Right to bail
a1-s12.plain: A person shall be released on bail by sufficient sureties, except in listed capital and violent or threatening felony cases. Excessive bail may not be required, the court must weigh listed factors in fixing bail, and may release a person on his or her own recognizance.
rights: shall be released on bail by sufficient sureties
powers: may be released on his or her own recognizance
limits: Excessive bail may not be required

a1-s13.title: Searches, seizures and warrants
a1-s13.plain: The right of the people to be secure in their persons, houses, papers, and effects against unreasonable seizures and searches may not be violated, and a warrant may issue only on probable cause, supported by oath or affirmation, particularly describing the place and the persons and things.
rights: The right of the people to be secure in their persons, houses, papers, and effects against unreasonable seizures and searches
limits: may not be violated
a warrant may not issue except on probable cause

a1-s14.title: Felony charges, magistrate and interpreter
a1-s14.plain: Felonies are prosecuted by indictment or, after examination and commitment by a magistrate, by information. A person charged by complaint shall be taken without unnecessary delay before a magistrate, who must inform the defendant of the right to counsel. A person unable to understand English charged with a crime has a right to an interpreter.
rights: shall be taken without unnecessary delay before a magistrate of that court
has a right to an interpreter throughout the proceedings

a1-s14.1.title: No preliminary hearing after indictment
a1-s14.1.plain: If a felony is prosecuted by indictment, there shall be no postindictment preliminary hearing.
limits: there shall be no postindictment preliminary hearing

a1-s15.title: Rights of the accused
a1-s15.plain: A criminal defendant has the right to a speedy public trial, to compel attendance of witnesses, to counsel, to be present with counsel, and to confront witnesses. No one may be twice put in jeopardy, compelled to be a witness against themselves, or deprived of life, liberty, or property without due process.
rights: the right to a speedy public trial
to compel attendance of witnesses
to have the assistance of counsel
to be personally present with counsel
to be confronted with the witnesses against the defendant
powers: The Legislature may provide for the deposition of a witness
limits: may not twice be put in jeopardy for the same offense
be compelled in a criminal cause to be a witness against themselves
be deprived of life, liberty, or property without due process of law

a1-s16.title: Trial by jury
a1-s16.plain: Trial by jury is an inviolate right secured to all, though three-fourths of a civil jury may render a verdict. It sets how a jury may be waived and the jury's size: 12 in felony cases, and 12 or fewer by agreement in civil and misdemeanor cases.
rights: Trial by jury is an inviolate right and shall be secured to all
powers: the Legislature may provide that the jury shall consist of eight persons or a lesser number

a1-s17.title: Cruel or unusual punishment and excessive fines
a1-s17.plain: Cruel or unusual punishment may not be inflicted, and excessive fines may not be imposed.
limits: Cruel or unusual punishment may not be inflicted
excessive fines imposed

a1-s18.title: Treason against the State
a1-s18.plain: Treason against the State consists only in levying war against it, adhering to its enemies, or giving them aid and comfort. A person may not be convicted of treason except on two witnesses to the same overt act or confession in open court.
limits: A person may not be convicted of treason except on the evidence of two witnesses to the same overt act or by confession in open court

a1-s19.title: Eminent domain and just compensation
a1-s19.plain: Private property may be taken or damaged for a public use and only when just compensation, ascertained by a jury unless waived, has first been paid. The State and local governments may not take an owner-occupied residence by eminent domain to convey it to a private person, with listed exceptions.
rights: just compensation
powers: The Legislature may provide for possession by the condemnor
limits: The State and local governments are prohibited from acquiring by eminent domain an owner-occupied residence for the purpose of conveying it to a private person

a1-s20.title: Property rights of noncitizens
a1-s20.plain: Noncitizens have the same property rights as citizens.
rights: the same property rights as citizens

a1-s21.title: Separate property
a1-s21.plain: Property owned before marriage, or acquired during marriage by gift, will, or inheritance, is separate property.

a1-s22.title: No property qualification to vote or hold office
a1-s22.plain: The right to vote or hold office may not be conditioned by a property qualification.
rights: The right to vote or hold office
limits: may not be conditioned by a property qualification

a1-s23.title: Grand juries
a1-s23.plain: One or more grand juries shall be drawn and summoned at least once a year in each county.

a1-s24.title: State rights independent; construing criminal rights
a1-s24.plain: California's constitutional rights do not depend on federal ones, but listed rights of criminal defendants shall be construed consistently with the U.S. Constitution, without greater rights for criminal defendants or minors in juvenile proceedings. This declaration does not impair others retained by the people.
limits: shall not be construed by the courts to afford greater rights to criminal defendants than those afforded by the Constitution of the United States
may not be construed to impair or deny others retained by the people

a1-s25.title: Right to fish
a1-s25.plain: The people have the right to fish on the State's public lands and waters, except fish hatchery lands. State land may not be sold without reserving that right, and entering public lands to fish in State-planted waters may not be made a crime; the legislature may set fishing seasons and conditions.
rights: the right to fish upon and from the public lands of the State and in the waters thereof
the absolute right to fish thereupon
powers: the legislature may by statute, provide for the season when and the conditions under which the different species of fish may be taken
limits: no land owned by the State shall ever be sold or transferred without reserving in the people
no law shall ever be passed making it a crime for the people to enter upon the public lands within this State for the purpose of fishing

a1-s26.title: Constitution is mandatory and prohibitory
a1-s26.plain: The provisions of this Constitution are mandatory and prohibitory, unless by express words they are declared to be otherwise.

a1-s27.title: Death penalty statutes
a1-s27.plain: Death penalty statutes in effect on February 17, 1972, are in full force, subject to amendment or repeal by statute, initiative, or referendum. The death penalty under them is not cruel or unusual punishment under Article 1, Section 6, nor contrary to any other provision of this constitution.

a1-s28.title: Victims' rights
a1-s28.plain: The People declare findings on crime victims. A victim is entitled to listed rights, including fairness and respect, protection, notice, being heard, a speedy trial, and restitution, which victims may enforce in court. It also sets shared rights to safe schools, truth-in-evidence, public safety bail, use of prior convictions, and truth in sentencing.
rights: To be treated with fairness and respect for his or her privacy and dignity
To be reasonably protected from the defendant
To be heard, upon request, at any proceeding
To a speedy trial and a prompt and final conclusion of the case
To restitution
the inalienable right to attend campuses which are safe, secure and peaceful
powers: may enforce the rights enumerated in subdivision (b)
The court in its discretion may extend the right to be heard at sentencing
limits: relevant evidence shall not be excluded in any criminal proceeding
Excessive bail may not be required
shall not be substantially diminished by early release policies

a1-s29.title: People's right to due process and speedy trial
a1-s29.plain: In a criminal case, the people of the State of California have the right to due process of law and to a speedy and public trial.
rights: the right to due process of law and to a speedy and public trial

a1-s30.title: Joinder, hearsay at preliminary hearings, discovery
a1-s30.plain: This Constitution shall not be construed to prohibit joining criminal cases. Hearsay evidence shall be admissible at preliminary hearings, and discovery in criminal cases shall be reciprocal, as prescribed by the Legislature or by the people through the initiative process.
limits: shall not be construed by the courts to prohibit the joining of criminal cases

a1-s31.title: No discrimination or preferential treatment
a1-s31.plain: The State shall not discriminate against, or grant preferential treatment to, any individual or group on the basis of race, sex, color, ethnicity, or national origin in public employment, public education, or public contracting, with listed exceptions.
limits: shall not discriminate against, or grant preferential treatment to, any individual or group

a1-s32.title: Parole consideration and credits
a1-s32.plain: A person convicted of a nonviolent felony and sentenced to state prison shall be eligible for parole consideration after completing the full term for the primary offense. The Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation may award credits and shall adopt regulations, which the Secretary shall certify protect and enhance public safety.
rights: shall be eligible for parole consideration after completing the full term for his or her primary offense
powers: shall have authority to award credits earned for good behavior and approved rehabilitative or educational achievements

a2-s1.title: Political power inherent in the people
a2-s1.plain: All political power is inherent in the people. Government is instituted for their protection, security, and benefit, and they have the right to alter or reform it when the public good may require.
rights: the right to alter or reform it

a2-s2.title: Who may vote
a2-s2.plain: A United States citizen 18 years of age and resident in this State may vote. An elector disqualified while serving a state or federal prison term shall have the right to vote restored when the prison term is completed.
rights: may vote
shall have their right to vote restored upon the completion of their prison term

a2-s2.5.title: Right to have vote counted
a2-s2.5.plain: A voter who casts a vote in an election in accordance with the laws of this State shall have that vote counted.
rights: shall have that vote counted

a2-s3.title: Residence, registration and free elections
a2-s3.plain: The Legislature shall define residence and provide for registration and free elections.

a2-s4.title: Improper election practices and disqualification of electors
a2-s4.plain: The Legislature shall prohibit improper practices that affect elections and shall provide for disqualifying electors while mentally incompetent or serving a state or federal prison term for a felony conviction.

a2-s5.title: Voter-nominated (top-two) primary elections
a2-s5.plain: A voter-nominated primary selects candidates for congressional and state offices; all voters may vote for any candidate regardless of party preference, and the top two compete in the general election. Parties may not nominate at that primary. The Legislature shall provide for partisan presidential and party elections.
rights: may vote at a voter-nominated primary election for any candidate
may have his or her political party preference, or lack of political party preference, indicated upon the ballot
has the right to participate in the general election for that office
limits: shall not nominate a candidate for any congressional or state elective office at the voter-nominated primary
shall not have the right to have its preferred candidate participate in the general election
shall not be denied the ability to place on the general election ballot the candidate

a2-s6.title: Nonpartisan offices
a2-s6.plain: All judicial, school, county, and city offices, including the Superintendent of Public Instruction, shall be nonpartisan. Parties shall not nominate candidates for nonpartisan office, and a candidate's party preference shall not be on the ballot.
limits: shall not nominate a candidate for nonpartisan office
shall not be included on the ballot for the nonpartisan office

a2-s7.title: Secret ballot
rights: Voting shall be secret

a2-s8.title: The initiative
a2-s8.plain: The initiative is the electors' power to propose and adopt or reject statutes and constitutional amendments, by petition signed by a set share of voters. The Secretary of State submits a qualified measure at an election. Measures may embrace only one subject and are limited in other ways.
powers: The initiative is the power of the electors to propose statutes and amendments to the Constitution and to adopt or reject them
may call a special statewide election for the measure
limits: may not be submitted to the electors or have any effect
may not include or exclude any political subdivision of the State from the application or effect of its provisions
may not contain alternative or cumulative provisions

a2-s9.title: The referendum
a2-s9.plain: The referendum is the electors' power to approve or reject statutes, except urgency statutes, statutes calling elections, and tax levy or usual current expense appropriation statutes. A petition signed by 5 percent of the last gubernatorial vote, filed within 90 days, puts the statute to the voters.
powers: The referendum is the power of the electors to approve or reject statutes or parts of statutes
may call a special statewide election for the measure
limits: the petition may not be presented on or after January 1 next following the enactment date

a2-s10.title: When measures take effect; amendment; petitions
a2-s10.plain: An approved initiative statute or referendum takes effect on the fifth day after the statement of the vote is filed. When approved measures conflict, the one with the most affirmative votes prevails. The Legislature may amend or repeal initiative statutes only with voter approval unless the initiative permits otherwise.
powers: The Legislature may amend or repeal a referendum statute
The Legislature may amend or repeal an initiative statute
limits: shall not be delayed from going into effect

a2-s11.title: Local initiative and referendum
a2-s11.plain: Electors of each city or county may exercise initiative and referendum powers under procedures the Legislature shall provide. City or county initiatives may not include or exclude parts of the area based on how they vote, or contain alternative or cumulative provisions depending on vote percentages.
powers: Initiative and referendum powers may be exercised by the electors of each city or county
limits: may not include or exclude any part of the city or county from the application or effect of its provisions
may not contain alternative or cumulative provisions

a2-s12.title: Measures naming individuals or corporations
a2-s12.plain: No constitutional amendment, and no statute proposed to the electors by the Legislature or by initiative, that names an individual to hold office or names a private corporation to perform a function or have a power or duty may be submitted to the electors or have any effect.
limits: No amendment to the Constitution, and no statute proposed to the electors

a2-s13.title: The recall
a2-s13.plain: Recall is the power of the electors to remove an elective officer.
powers: Recall is the power of the electors to remove an elective officer

a2-s14.title: Recall petitions for state officers
a2-s14.plain: Recall of a state officer starts with a petition to the Secretary of State alleging a reason, which is not reviewable; proponents have 160 days to file. It sets signature thresholds for statewide and other officers, and the Secretary of State keeps a continuous count.
limits: Sufficiency of reason is not reviewable

a2-s15.title: Recall elections
a2-s15.plain: The Governor shall call a recall election within 60 to 80 days of certification, or within 180 days to consolidate with a regular election. If a majority votes to recall, the officer is removed and the plurality candidate succeeds; the officer may not be a candidate.
powers: A recall election may be conducted within 180 days
limits: The officer may not be a candidate

a2-s16.title: Legislature to provide for recall procedures
a2-s16.plain: The Legislature shall provide for circulation, filing, and certification of petitions, nomination of candidates, and the recall election.

a2-s17.title: Recall of Governor or Secretary of State
a2-s17.plain: If recall of the Governor or Secretary of State is initiated, the Lieutenant Governor or Controller, respectively, shall perform the recall duties of that office.

a2-s18.title: Reimbursement and repeat recalls
a2-s18.plain: A state officer who is not recalled shall be reimbursed by the State for recall election expenses legally and personally incurred. Another recall may not be initiated against the officer until six months after the election.
rights: shall be reimbursed by the State for the officer’s recall election expenses legally and personally incurred
limits: Another recall may not be initiated against the officer

a2-s19.title: Recall of local officers
a2-s19.plain: The Legislature shall provide for recall of local officers. This section does not affect counties and cities whose charters provide for recall.

a2-s20.title: Start of terms of elective offices
a2-s20.plain: Terms of elective offices provided for by this Constitution, other than Members of the Legislature, commence on the Monday after January 1 following election. The election is held in the last even-numbered year before the term expires.

a3-s1.title: California part of the United States
a3-s1.plain: The State of California is an inseparable part of the United States of America, and the United States Constitution is the supreme law of the land.

a3-s2.title: State boundaries and capital
a3-s2.plain: The State's boundaries are those stated in the Constitution of 1849 as modified pursuant to statute. Sacramento is the capital of California.

a3-s3.title: Separation of powers
a3-s3.plain: The powers of state government are legislative, executive, and judicial. Persons charged with exercising one power may not exercise either of the others except as this Constitution permits.
limits: may not exercise either of the others

a3-s3.5.title: Administrative agencies and unconstitutional statutes
a3-s3.5.plain: An administrative agency has no power to declare a statute unconstitutional, or to declare a statute unenforceable or refuse to enforce it as unconstitutional or barred by federal law, unless an appellate court has so determined.
limits: has no power

a3-s4.title: Salaries of elected state officers and judges
a3-s4.plain: Salaries of elected state officers may not be reduced during their term. Judges' base salaries are fixed from January 1, 1981; the Legislature may raise them or end prospective increases but shall not reduce a judge's salary during a term below the highest level paid.
powers: The Legislature may prescribe increases in those salaries during a term of office
may terminate prospective increases in those salaries at any time during a term of office
limits: salaries of elected state officers may not be reduced during their term of office
shall not reduce the salary of a judge during a term of office below the highest level paid during that term of office

a3-s5.title: Suits against the State
a3-s5.plain: Suits may be brought against the State in the manner and in the courts directed by law.

a3-s6.title: English as the official language
a3-s6.plain: English is the official language of California. The Legislature shall enforce this section and make no law that diminishes or ignores the role of English. Residents and those doing business in California may sue the State to enforce it.
rights: shall have standing to sue the State of California to enforce this section
powers: shall have jurisdiction to hear cases brought to enforce this section
The Legislature may provide reasonable and appropriate limitations on the time and manner of suits brought under this section
limits: shall make no law which diminishes or ignores the role of English as the common language of the State of California

a3-s7.title: Retirement allowances of certain elective officers
a3-s7.plain: Legislators' Retirement System allowances of certain elective state officers (not judges or legislators), and of their survivors or beneficiaries, shall not be increased or affected by compensation changes on or after November 5, 1986. It states the people's intent and findings against windfall benefits.
limits: shall not be increased or affected in any manner by changes on or after November 5, 1986, in the compensation payable

a3-s8.title: California Citizens Compensation Commission
a3-s8.plain: Creates a seven-member commission appointed by the Governor that establishes and adjusts the annual salary and medical, dental, insurance and similar benefits of state officers by majority resolution, sets who may serve, requires open meetings, and lists factors it shall consider.
limits: No current or former officer or employee of this State is eligible for appointment to the commission
a resolution shall not be adopted or take effect in any year that increases the annual salary of any state officer

a3-s9.title: Proceeds from sale of surplus state property
a3-s9.plain: Proceeds from selling surplus state property shall be used to pay principal and interest on Economic Recovery Bond Act bonds; once those are paid, the proceeds shall go into the Special Fund for Economic Uncertainties or any successor fund.

a4-s1.title: Legislative power; initiative and referendum
a4-s1.plain: The legislative power of California is vested in the California Legislature, made up of the Senate and Assembly, but the people reserve to themselves the powers of initiative and referendum.
powers: The legislative power of this State is vested in the California Legislature
the people reserve to themselves the powers of initiative and referendum

a4-s1.5.title: Findings on incumbency and term limits
a4-s1.5.plain: The people find that incumbents' unlimited terms, own retirement system, and state-paid staff create career politicians, and declare that the powers of incumbency must be limited: retirement benefits restricted, staff and support services limited, and terms limited.

a4-s2.title: Legislature membership, terms and qualifications
a4-s2.plain: The Senate has 40 members with 4-year terms and the Assembly 80 with 2-year terms. A person may serve no more than 12 years in the Legislature. Members must be electors and meet residence and citizenship requirements. The Governor shall call an election to fill a vacancy.
limits: a person may serve no more than 12 years in the Senate, the Assembly, or both
A person is ineligible to be a member of the Legislature

a4-s3.title: Regular and special sessions
a4-s3.plain: The Legislature shall convene in regular session on the first Monday in December of each even-numbered year and adjourns at midnight on November 30 two years later. The Governor may call a special session, limited to subjects in the proclamation and incidental matters.
powers: the Governor by proclamation may cause the Legislature to assemble in special session
may provide for expenses and other matters incidental to the session
limits: has power to legislate only on subjects specified in the proclamation

a4-s4.title: Legislators' outside income, travel expenses and retirement
a4-s4.plain: No Member may knowingly receive earned income from a lobbyist, lobbying firm or recent legislative contractor. Travel and living expenses are set by two-thirds statute and limited during long recesses. Legislative retirement benefits are limited.
powers: The Legislature may, prior to their retirement, limit the retirement benefits payable to Members of the Legislature
the Legislature may provide that no Member shall be deprived of a cost of living adjustment
limits: no Member of the Legislature may knowingly receive any salary, wages, commissions, or other similar earned income from a lobbyist or lobbying firm
may not, for a period of one year following its receipt, vote upon
A Member may not receive travel and living expenses during the times that the Legislature is in recess for more than three calendar days
The Legislature may not provide retirement benefits based on any portion of a monthly salary in excess of five hundred dollars ($500)

a4-s4.5.title: Legislators' Social Security; no other pension
a4-s4.5.plain: A person elected to or serving in the Legislature on or after November 1, 1990, shall participate in Social Security, with the State paying only the employer's share. No other pension or retirement benefit shall accrue from legislative service, though vested benefits are not diminished.
limits: No other pension or retirement benefit shall accrue as a result of service in the Legislature
no further entitlement to nor vesting in any existing program shall accrue to any such person

a4-s5.title: Discipline and ethics of Members
a4-s5.plain: Each house judges its Members' qualifications and elections and, by two-thirds rollcall vote, may expel or suspend a Member. Members may not accept honoraria or compensation for appearing before state boards or agencies, and the Legislature shall enact laws on gifts, lobbying and conflicts of interest.
powers: may expel a Member
Each house may suspend a Member
the house may deem the salary and benefits of the Member to be forfeited
the people reserve to themselves the power to implement this requirement
limits: shall not exercise any of the rights, privileges, duties, or powers of his or her office
No Member of the Legislature may accept any honorarium

No Member of the Legislature may knowingly accept any compensation for appearing, agreeing to appear, or taking any other action on behalf of another person before any state government board or agency
the Member may not, for a period of one year following the acceptance of the compensation, vote upon

a4-s6.title: Senate and Assembly districts
a4-s6.plain: For choosing members of the Legislature, the State is divided into 40 Senatorial and 80 Assembly districts; each Senatorial district chooses one Senator and each Assembly district one member of the Assembly.

a4-s7.title: Legislative proceedings, journals and open sessions
a4-s7.plain: Each house chooses its officers, adopts rules and keeps a journal. Proceedings shall be open and public, and any person may record and broadcast them; the Legislature shall post recordings online. Closed sessions are allowed only for listed purposes and party caucuses.
rights: The right to attend open and public proceedings
the right of any person to record by audio or video means any and all parts of the proceedings
shall have standing to challenge said rules
powers: may recess from day to day and compel the attendance of absent members
the Legislature may adopt reasonable rules pursuant to paragraph (5)
closed sessions may be held solely for any of the following purposes
may meet in closed session
limits: Neither house without the consent of the other may recess for more than 10 days or to any other place

a4-s7.5.title: Limit on Legislature's spending
a4-s7.5.plain: The Legislature's total spending on member and employee compensation and operating expenses may not exceed, in the first fiscal year after adoption, $950,000 per member or 80 percent of the prior year's amount, whichever is less; afterward, the prior year's amount adjusted by the State appropriations limit.
limits: may not exceed an amount equal to nine hundred fifty thousand dollars ($950,000) per member
the total aggregate expenditures may not exceed an amount equal to that expended for those purposes in the preceding fiscal year

a4-s8.title: Passing bills; when statutes take effect
a4-s8.plain: At regular sessions no bill but the budget bill may be acted on until the 31st day after introduction. Bills must be read on 3 days, published online 72 hours before the vote, and passed by a majority of each house. It sets when statutes take effect.
powers: the house may dispense with this requirement
limits: no bill other than the budget bill may be heard or acted on by committee or either house until the 31st day after the bill is introduced
The Legislature may make no law except by statute and may enact no statute except by bill
No bill may be passed unless it is read by title on 3 days in each house
No bill may be passed or ultimately become a statute unless the bill with any amendments has been printed, distributed to the members, and published on the Internet
No bill may be passed unless, by rollcall vote entered in the journal, a majority of the membership of each house concurs
An urgency statute may not create or abolish any office

a4-s8.5.title: Limits on measures submitted to voters
a4-s8.5.plain: An act amending an initiative statute, a bond act, or a legislative constitutional amendment submitted to voters may not include or exclude a political subdivision based on how its electors vote, or contain alternative or cumulative provisions that depend on a specified percentage of votes.
limits: Include or exclude any political subdivision of the State from the application or effect of its provisions
Contain alternative or cumulative provisions

a4-s9.title: Single subject and amending statutes
a4-s9.plain: A statute shall embrace but one subject, expressed in its title; any part whose subject is not expressed in the title is void. A statute may not be amended by reference to its title, and a section may not be amended unless re-enacted as amended.
limits: A statute shall embrace but one subject
A statute may not be amended by reference to its title
A section of a statute may not be amended unless the section is re-enacted as amended

a4-s10.title: Governor's signature, veto and bill deadlines
a4-s10.plain: Bills passed by the Legislature go to the Governor, who may sign or veto them; two-thirds of each house may override. It sets when unreturned bills become statutes, deadlines for passing bills, item reductions in appropriations, and fiscal emergency special sessions.
powers: The Governor may veto it by returning it with any objections to the house of origin
The Governor may reduce or eliminate one or more items of appropriation while approving other portions of a bill
the Governor may issue a proclamation declaring a fiscal emergency
limits: may no longer be acted on by the house
No bill may be passed by either house on or after September 1 of an even-numbered year
The Legislature may not present any bill to the Governor after November 15 of the second calendar year of the biennium of the legislative session
the Legislature may not act on any other bill, nor may the Legislature adjourn for a joint recess

a4-s11.title: Legislative committees
a4-s11.plain: The Legislature or either house may by resolution provide for selecting committees needed for its business, including committees to find facts and make recommendations on subjects within legislative control.
powers: may by resolution provide for the selection of committees necessary for the conduct of its business

a4-s12.title: State budget and budget bill
a4-s12.plain: The Governor must submit a budget each January with a budget bill. The Legislature must pass the budget bill by midnight June 15 by majority vote. It limits other appropriations, bars an unbalanced budget bill, and stops legislators' pay when the budget is late.
powers: may require a state agency, officer or employee to furnish whatever information is deemed necessary to prepare the budget
The Legislature may control the submission, approval, and enforcement of budgets and the filing of claims for all state agencies
limits: the Legislature shall not send to the Governor for consideration any bill appropriating funds for expenditure during the fiscal year for which the budget bill is to be enacted
No bill except the budget bill may contain more than one item of appropriation
are void unless passed in each house by rollcall vote entered in the journal, two-thirds of the membership concurring
the Legislature may not send to the Governor for consideration, nor may the Governor sign into law, a budget bill that would appropriate from the General Fund
there shall be no appropriation from the current budget or future budget to pay any salary or reimbursement for travel or living expenses for Members of the Legislature
No salary or reimbursement for travel or living expenses forfeited pursuant to this subdivision shall be paid retroactively

a4-s12.5.title: Director of Finance revenue and spending estimates
a4-s12.5.plain: After the Governor's budget is submitted, after proposed adjustments to it, and after the budget bill is enacted, the Director of Finance must give the Legislature General Fund revenue and expenditure estimates for the ensuing fiscal year and the three years after.

a4-s13.title: Legislators may not hold other state office
a4-s13.plain: During the term for which they are elected, members of the Legislature may not hold any office or employment under the State other than an elective office.
limits: may not, during the term for which the member is elected, hold any office or employment under the State

a4-s14.title: Legislators exempt from civil process during session
a4-s14.plain: A member of the Legislature is not subject to civil process during a session of the Legislature or for 5 days before and after a session.
rights: is not subject to civil process during a session of the Legislature or for 5 days before and after a session

a4-s15.title: Bribing or improperly influencing legislators
a4-s15.plain: A person who seeks to influence a legislator's vote or action by bribery, promise of reward, intimidation, or other dishonest means, and a legislator so influenced, is guilty of a felony.
limits: is guilty of a felony

a4-s16.title: Uniform general laws; special statutes
a4-s16.plain: All laws of a general nature have uniform operation. A local or special statute is invalid in any case if a general statute can be made applicable.
limits: A local or special statute is invalid in any case

a4-s17.title: No extra pay after service is rendered
a4-s17.plain: The Legislature has no power to grant, or let local public bodies grant, extra compensation to a public officer, employee, or contractor after the service or contract is performed, or to authorize payment of a claim under an agreement made without authority of law.
limits: has no power to grant, or to authorize a city, county, or other public body to grant, extra compensation or extra allowance
or to authorize the payment of a claim against the State or a city, county, or other public body under an agreement made without authority of law

a4-s18.title: Impeachment
a4-s18.plain: The Assembly has the sole power of impeachment and the Senate tries impeachments; conviction needs two thirds of the Senate. Statewide elected officers, Board of Equalization members, and state judges may be impeached for misconduct; judgment is limited to removal and disqualification.
powers: The Assembly has the sole power of impeachment
limits: A person may not be convicted unless, by rollcall vote entered in the journal, two thirds of the membership of the Senate concurs
Judgment may extend only to removal from office and disqualification to hold any office under the State

a4-s19.title: Lotteries, gambling and tribal gaming
a4-s19.plain: The Legislature has no power to authorize lotteries or Nevada- and New Jersey-type casinos and shall prohibit them, but a California State Lottery is authorized, and horse racing, charitable bingo and raffles, and compact-based tribal gaming on Indian lands may be allowed.
powers: The Legislature may provide for the regulation of horse races and horse race meetings and wagering on the results
the Legislature by statute may authorize cities and counties to provide for bingo games
there is authorized the establishment of a California State Lottery
the Governor is authorized to negotiate and conclude compacts
the Legislature may authorize private, nonprofit, eligible organizations, as defined by the Legislature, to conduct raffles
may amend the percentage of gross receipts required by this subdivision to be dedicated to beneficial or charitable purposes
limits: The Legislature has no power to authorize lotteries
The Legislature has no power to authorize,

a4-s20.title: Fish and game; Fish and Game Commission
a4-s20.plain: The Legislature may divide the State into fish and game districts and protect fish and game. A 5-member Fish and Game Commission is appointed by the Governor and approved by the Senate for 6-year terms; the Legislature may delegate powers to it.
powers: The Legislature may provide for division of the State into fish and game districts
may protect fish and game in districts or parts of districts
The Legislature may delegate to the commission such powers relating to the protection and propagation of fish and game
may be removed by concurrent resolution adopted by each house

a4-s21.title: War-caused or enemy-caused disaster
a4-s21.plain: To meet needs from war-caused or enemy-caused disaster in California, the Legislature may provide for filling legislative seats and the Governor's office, convening the Legislature, holding elections for vacant offices, and choosing a temporary seat of state or county government.
powers: the Legislature may provide for

a4-s22.title: Right to hold legislators accountable
a4-s22.plain: The people have the right to hold their legislators accountable. To assist them, legislative leaders of each house shall report the house's goals at the start of each regular session and its progress at the close.
rights: the right of the people to hold their legislators accountable

a4-s28.title: State Capitol restoration spending
a4-s28.plain: No bill appropriating money to alter the historically restored areas of the State Capitol, or to replace their period furniture, may take effect as an urgency statute, and no such spending may be made unless funds are expressly appropriated. Ordinary repair and maintenance is excepted.
limits: no bill shall take effect as an urgency statute
No expenditures shall be made in payment for any of the purposes described in subdivision (a) of this section

a5-s1.title: Executive power vested in the Governor
a5-s1.plain: The supreme executive power of California is vested in the Governor, who shall see that the law is faithfully executed.
powers: The supreme executive power of this State is vested in the Governor

a5-s2.title: Governor's election, term and qualifications
a5-s2.plain: The Governor is elected every fourth year with Assembly members and serves until a successor qualifies. The Governor must be an elector who has been a U.S. citizen and state resident for 5 years, may not hold other public office, and may serve no more than 2 terms.
limits: The Governor may not hold other public office
No Governor may serve more than 2 terms

a5-s3.title: Governor's yearly report to the Legislature
a5-s3.plain: Each calendar year the Governor shall report to the Legislature on the condition of the State and may make recommendations.
powers: may make recommendations

a5-s4.title: Governor may require information
a5-s4.plain: The Governor may require executive officers and agencies and their employees to furnish information relating to their duties.
powers: may require executive officers and agencies and their employees to furnish information relating to their duties

a5-s5.title: Filling vacancies in office
a5-s5.plain: Unless the law provides otherwise, the Governor may fill a vacancy by appointment. For vacancies in listed statewide offices or the Board of Equalization, the Governor nominates a person who takes office when confirmed by both houses, or if neither confirmed nor refused within 90 days.
powers: the Governor may fill a vacancy in office by appointment

a5-s6.title: Reorganizing executive functions
a5-s6.plain: A statute may give the Governor authority to assign and reorganize functions among executive officers and agencies and their employees, other than elective officers and agencies they administer.
powers: Authority may be provided by statute for the Governor to assign and reorganize functions among executive officers and agencies and their employees

a5-s7.title: Governor as commander in chief of the militia
a5-s7.plain: The Governor is commander in chief of a militia that shall be provided by statute, and may call it forth to execute the law.
powers: The Governor is commander in chief of a militia
The Governor may call it forth to execute the law

a5-s8.title: Pardons, reprieves and review of parole
a5-s8.plain: The Governor may grant reprieves, pardons and commutations after sentence, except in impeachment, and must report each to the Legislature. Parole decisions for murder sentences wait 30 days so the Governor may affirm, modify or reverse them.
powers: may grant a reprieve, pardon, and commutation, after sentence
the Governor may review the decision
limits: The Governor may not grant a pardon or commutation to a person twice convicted of a felony
may only affirm, modify, or reverse the decision of the parole authority on the basis of the same factors

a5-s9.title: Lieutenant Governor's qualifications and Senate role
a5-s9.plain: The Lieutenant Governor must have the same qualifications as the Governor, and is President of the Senate but has only a casting vote.
limits: has only a casting vote

a5-s10.title: Succession to the office of Governor
a5-s10.plain: The Lieutenant Governor becomes Governor when the office is vacant and acts as Governor during the Governor's impeachment, absence or temporary disability. The Legislature sets the further order of succession, and the Supreme Court decides all questions under this section.
powers: The Supreme Court has exclusive jurisdiction to determine all questions arising under this section
Standing to raise questions of vacancy or temporary disability is vested exclusively in a body provided by statute

a5-s11.title: Election and term limits of statewide officers
a5-s11.plain: The Lieutenant Governor, Attorney General, Controller, Secretary of State and Treasurer are elected at the same time and places and for the same term as the Governor, and none may serve in the same office for more than 2 terms.
limits: may serve in the same office for more than 2 terms

a5-s13.title: Attorney General as chief law officer
a5-s13.plain: Subject to the Governor, the Attorney General is the State's chief law officer, must see that the laws are uniformly and adequately enforced, supervises district attorneys and sheriffs, and may prosecute violations in a county where a law is not adequately enforced.
powers: shall have direct supervision over every district attorney and sheriff
may require any of said officers to make reports
the Attorney General shall have all the powers of a district attorney

a5-s14.title: Limits on state officers' income, honoraria and gifts
a5-s14.plain: State officers may not knowingly take earned income from lobbyists or certain state contractors, accept honoraria, or accept pay to appear before state boards or agencies. The Legislature must enact laws on gifts and post-office lobbying.
limits: no state officer may knowingly receive any salary, wages, commissions, or other similar earned income from a lobbyist or lobbying firm
No state officer may accept any honorarium
No state officer may knowingly accept any compensation for appearing, agreeing to appear, or taking any other action on behalf of another person before any state government board or agency

a6-s1.title: Judicial power of the State
a6-s1.plain: The judicial power of the State is vested in the Supreme Court, courts of appeal and superior courts, all of which are courts of record.
powers: The judicial power of this State is vested in the Supreme Court, courts of appeal, and superior courts

a6-s2.title: The Supreme Court
a6-s2.plain: The Supreme Court has the Chief Justice and 6 associate justices; the Chief Justice may convene it at any time, and a judgment needs 4 judges concurring. An acting Chief Justice serves when the Chief Justice is absent or unable to act.
powers: The Chief Justice may convene the court at any time

a6-s3.title: Courts of appeal
a6-s3.plain: The Legislature shall divide the State into court of appeal districts. Each division has a presiding justice and 2 or more associate justices, sits as a 3-judge court, and needs 2 judges concurring for a judgment.
powers: It has the power of a court of appeal

a6-s4.title: Superior courts and appellate divisions
a6-s4.plain: Each county has a superior court of one or more judges, with an appellate division. The Legislature sets the number of judges and may, if each affected county concurs, have judges serve more than one superior court.
powers: the Legislature may provide that one or more judges serve more than one superior court

a6-s6.title: The Judicial Council
a6-s6.plain: Sets the membership of the Judicial Council, which surveys judicial business, makes recommendations and adopts rules of court consistent with statute. The Chief Justice seeks to expedite and equalize judges' work and may assign judges to other courts.
powers: The council may appoint an Administrative Director of the Courts
The Chief Justice may provide for the assignment of any judge to another court
limits: The rules adopted shall not be inconsistent with statute

a6-s7.title: Commission on Judicial Appointments
a6-s7.plain: The Commission on Judicial Appointments consists of the Chief Justice, the Attorney General, and the presiding justice of the affected court of appeal district who has presided longest, or for the Supreme Court, the longest-serving presiding justice of any court of appeal.

a6-s8.title: Commission on Judicial Performance
a6-s8.plain: The Commission on Judicial Performance has judges, State Bar members and citizens appointed by the Supreme Court, Governor, Senate Committee on Rules and Speaker. Terms are four years, no member serves more than two terms, and staggered first terms began March 1, 1995.
limits: No member shall serve more than two four-year terms
may not appoint them to an additional term thereafter

a6-s9.title: The State Bar of California
a6-s9.plain: The State Bar of California is a public corporation. Every person admitted and licensed to practice law in the State is a member, except while serving as a judge of a court of record.

a6-s10.title: Original jurisdiction of the courts
a6-s10.plain: The Supreme Court, courts of appeal, superior courts and their judges have original jurisdiction in habeas corpus and in mandamus, certiorari and prohibition proceedings. Superior courts have original jurisdiction in all other causes, and a court may comment on the evidence and witnesses.
powers: have original jurisdiction in habeas corpus proceedings
Those courts also have original jurisdiction in proceedings for extraordinary relief
The appellate division of the superior court has original jurisdiction
Superior courts have original jurisdiction in all other causes
The court may make any comment on the evidence and the testimony and credibility of any witness

a6-s11.title: Appellate jurisdiction
a6-s11.plain: The Supreme Court has appellate jurisdiction when a death judgment is pronounced; courts of appeal and the superior court's appellate division hear other appeals as the text and statute provide. The Legislature may change the jurisdictional amount and let appellate courts take evidence.
powers: The Supreme Court has appellate jurisdiction
courts of appeal have appellate jurisdiction
the Legislature may change the appellate jurisdiction of the courts of appeal
the appellate division of the superior court has appellate jurisdiction in causes prescribed by statute
The Legislature may permit courts exercising appellate jurisdiction to take evidence and make findings of fact

a6-s12.title: Supreme Court transfer and review
a6-s12.plain: Before decision, the Supreme Court may transfer a cause from a court of appeal to itself, or from itself or one court of appeal to another, and may review any court of appeal decision. This section does not apply to death-judgment appeals.
powers: may, before decision, transfer to itself a cause in a court of appeal
transfer a cause from itself to a court of appeal or from one court of appeal or division to another
The Supreme Court may review the decision of a court of appeal in any cause

a6-s13.title: Judgments not set aside for harmless error
a6-s13.plain: No judgment may be set aside or new trial granted for jury misdirection, evidence rulings, or errors of pleading or procedure unless, after examining the entire cause, the court finds the error resulted in a miscarriage of justice.
limits: No judgment shall be set aside, or new trial granted

a6-s14.title: Publication and written decisions
a6-s14.plain: The Legislature must provide for prompt publication of the Supreme Court and courts of appeal opinions the Supreme Court deems appropriate, which any person may publish. Decisions that determine causes must be in writing with reasons stated.
rights: those opinions shall be available for publication by any person

a6-s15.title: Qualifications of judges
a6-s15.plain: A person cannot be a judge of a court of record unless, for the 10 years just before selection, the person was a State Bar member or a judge of a court of record in California.

a6-s16.title: Election and terms of judges
a6-s16.plain: Supreme Court and court of appeal judges are elected for 12-year terms, and superior court judges for six-year terms. Appellate judges run unopposed in yes-or-no retention elections, the Governor fills appellate vacancies subject to confirmation, and county electors may adopt that system for superior courts.
powers: may provide for their election by the system prescribed in subdivision (d), or by any other arrangement
The Legislature may provide that an unopposed incumbent’s name not appear on the ballot
may file a declaration of candidacy to succeed to the office presently held by the judge
may make this system of selection applicable to judges of superior courts
limits: only the candidate so declared or nominated may appear on the ballot
A candidate not elected may not be appointed to that court

a6-s17.title: Judges barred from other work and office
a6-s17.plain: A judge of a court of record may not practice law or, during the term, hold other public office or employment except part-time teaching; a trial judge may run for other office after taking unpaid leave. Judicial officers may not keep fines or fees or earn teaching retirement credit.
limits: may not practice law
is ineligible for public employment or public office other than judicial employment or judicial office
may not receive fines or fees for personal use
may not earn retirement service credit from a public teaching position

a6-s18.title: Discipline and removal of judges
a6-s18.plain: Judges are disqualified while facing felony charges or review of their removal. The Commission on Judicial Performance may disqualify, retire, censure, remove or admonish judges, must suspend and remove judges convicted of serious crimes, and the Supreme Court may review its decisions.
rights: shall be absolutely immune from suit
powers: may disqualify a judge from acting as a judge
retire a judge for disability
censure a judge or former judge or remove a judge
publicly or privately admonish a judge or former judge
The commission may also bar a former judge who has been censured from receiving an assignment, appointment, or reference of work
the Supreme Court may, in its discretion, grant review
it may make an independent review of the record
The State Bar may institute appropriate attorney disciplinary proceedings
The commission may provide for the confidentiality of complaints
The commission may make explanatory statements
limits: A judge is disqualified from acting as a judge
No court, except the Supreme Court, shall have jurisdiction
No civil action may be maintained against a person

a6-s18.1.title: Discipline of subordinate judicial officers
a6-s18.1.plain: The Commission on Judicial Performance oversees and disciplines subordinate judicial officers under the same standards and review as Section 18. A person found unfit after a commission hearing cannot serve as one, and courts keep initial authority to discipline or dismiss them.
limits: shall have the requisite status to serve as a subordinate judicial officer

a6-s18.5.title: Sharing judicial discipline records
a6-s18.5.plain: On request, the Commission on Judicial Performance must give a state governor, the President or the Commission on Judicial Appointments its disciplinary records on a judicial applicant. The information stays confidential but is also given to the applicant.
rights: shall also be provided to the applicant about whom the information was requested

a6-s19.title: Judges' pay and undecided cases
a6-s19.plain: The Legislature must set the pay of judges of courts of record. A judge may not receive salary while any cause before the judge stays undecided for 90 days after submission.
limits: may not receive the salary for the judicial office held by the judge

a6-s20.title: Retirement of judges
a6-s20.plain: The Legislature must provide for the retirement of judges of courts of record, with reasonable allowance, for age or disability.

a6-s21.title: Temporary judges
a6-s21.plain: If the parties agree, the court may order a cause tried by a temporary judge who is a State Bar member, sworn and empowered to act until the cause is finally determined.
powers: may order a cause to be tried by a temporary judge

a6-s22.title: Court commissioners
a6-s22.plain: The Legislature may provide for trial courts of record to appoint officers such as commissioners to perform subordinate judicial duties.
powers: The Legislature may provide for the appointment by trial courts of record of officers such as commissioners

a7-s1.title: The civil service
a7-s1.plain: The civil service includes every state officer and employee unless the Constitution provides otherwise. Permanent appointments and promotions are made under a merit system based on competitive examination.

a7-s2.title: The State Personnel Board
a7-s2.plain: A 5-member Personnel Board is appointed by the Governor and approved by the Senate for 10-year terms, and members may be removed by a two-thirds vote of each house. The board elects a presiding officer and appoints an executive officer.
powers: A member may be removed by concurrent resolution adopted by each house

a7-s3.title: Duties of the Personnel Board
a7-s3.plain: The board must enforce the civil service statutes and, by majority vote of all members, set probationary periods and classifications, adopt rules authorized by statute, and review disciplinary actions. The executive officer administers the statutes under board rules.

a7-s4.title: Positions exempt from civil service
a7-s4.plain: Lists positions exempt from civil service, including legislative and judicial branch staff, elected officers and their deputies, board members, Governor's appointees, university staff, teachers and militia members. The Attorney General, Public Utilities Commission and Legislative Counsel may also appoint a few exempt deputies or employees.
powers: the Attorney General may appoint or employ six deputies or employees
the Public Utilities Commission may appoint or employ one deputy or employee
the Legislative Counsel may appoint or employ two deputies or employees

a7-s5.title: Temporary appointments
a7-s5.plain: A temporary appointment may be made to a position with no employment list, but no one may serve under temporary appointment longer than 9 months in 12 consecutive months.
limits: may serve in one or more positions under temporary appointment longer than 9 months in 12 consecutive months

a7-s6.title: Veterans' preference and continuing employees
a7-s6.plain: The Legislature may provide preferences for veterans and their surviving spouses. The board may let people in positions newly brought under civil service qualify to stay, and must do so for workers whose work the State takes over.
powers: The Legislature may provide preferences for veterans and their surviving spouses
may permit persons in exempt positions, brought under civil service by constitutional provision, to qualify to continue in their positions

a7-s7.title: No dual lucrative offices
a7-s7.plain: A person holding a lucrative office under the United States or other power may not hold a civil office of profit. Low-paid local officers and postmasters, militia officers and most military reservists do not hold lucrative offices for this purpose.
limits: may not hold a civil office of profit

a7-s8.title: Disqualification for bribery and other crimes
a7-s8.plain: A person convicted of giving or offering a bribe to get elected or appointed is disqualified from any office of profit. Laws must exclude those convicted of bribery, perjury and other high crimes from office and juries, and protect free suffrage against undue influence.
rights: The privilege of free suffrage
limits: shall be disqualified from holding any office of profit in this State

a7-s9.title: Advocates of violent overthrow barred
a7-s9.plain: Notwithstanding the rest of the Constitution, no person or organization advocating the violent or unlawful overthrow of the U.S. or state government, or support of a foreign enemy in hostilities, may hold public office or employment or receive a tax exemption. The Legislature must enforce this.
limits: Hold any office or employment under this State
Receive any exemption from any tax imposed by this State

a7-s10.title: Office lost for libel or slander of an opponent
a7-s10.plain: A person found civilly liable for libel or slander of an opposing candidate that was a major contributing cause of that candidate's defeat shall not retain the seat won. The trier of fact makes a separate written finding, and the office becomes vacant.
limits: shall be disqualified from or shall forfeit that office
shall have no authority to exercise the powers or perform the duties of the office

a7-s11.title: Limits on legislators' and judges' retirement pay
a7-s11.plain: For people who first entered a covered state or judicial office on or after January 1, 1987, the Legislators’ and Judges’ Retirement Systems shall not pay a retirement allowance above the higher of the current salary for that office or the retiree's highest salary in it.
powers: The Legislature may define the terms used in this section
limits: The Legislators’ Retirement System shall not pay any unmodified retirement allowance
The Judges’ Retirement System shall not pay any unmodified retirement allowance

a9-s1.title: Promotion of knowledge
a9-s1.plain: Because a general diffusion of knowledge and intelligence is essential to preserving the people's rights and liberties, the Legislature shall encourage by all suitable means intellectual, scientific, moral, and agricultural improvement.

a9-s2.title: Superintendent of Public Instruction
a9-s2.plain: The Superintendent of Public Instruction is elected by the State's voters at each gubernatorial election and takes office the first Monday after January 1 following the election. No Superintendent may serve more than 2 terms.
limits: No Superintendent of Public Instruction may serve more than 2 terms

a9-s2.1.title: Deputy and Associate Superintendents
a9-s2.1.plain: On the Superintendent of Public Instruction's nomination, the State Board of Education appoints one Deputy and three Associate Superintendents, exempt from state civil service, for four-year terms. Additional civil-service Associate Superintendents may still be appointed in accordance with law.
powers: shall appoint one Deputy Superintendent of Public Instruction and three Associate Superintendents of Public Instruction

a9-s3.title: County superintendents of schools
a9-s3.plain: A county superintendent of schools may be elected by the county's voters or appointed by the county board of education, as a majority of the county's voters decide. Two or more counties may unite to elect or appoint one joint superintendent.
powers: may be appointed by the county board of education
unite for the purpose of electing or appointing one joint superintendent

a9-s3.1.title: County superintendent qualifications and salary
a9-s3.1.plain: The Legislature shall prescribe the qualifications of county superintendents of schools and classify the counties for that purpose. The county board of education, or joint county board, fixes the superintendent's salary.
powers: shall fix the salary of the county superintendent of schools or the joint county superintendent of schools

a9-s3.2.title: Joint county boards and superintendents
a9-s3.2.plain: Two or more counties may, by a majority vote of each county's voters, establish one joint board of education and one joint county superintendent of schools. These are governed by the general statutes, not by any county charter.
powers: establish one joint board of education and one joint county superintendent of schools
limits: shall not be governed by the provisions of any county charter

a9-s3.3.title: County boards of education under county charters
a9-s3.3.plain: Except as provided in Section 3.2 of this article, a county charter, or an amendment to it, may provide for the election of the members of the county board of education and for their qualifications and terms of office.
powers: it shall be competent to provide in any charter framed for a county

a9-s5.title: System of common schools
a9-s5.plain: The Legislature shall provide for a system of common schools under which a free school is kept up and supported in each district at least six months every year after a school's first year there.

a9-s6.title: Teacher pay, Public School System and School Fund
a9-s6.plain: Sets a minimum $2,400 annual salary for full-time certificated school employees, defines the Public School System and bars transferring any part of it out, and requires minimum per-pupil and per-district amounts from the State School Fund.
rights: shall be paid a salary which shall be at the rate of an annual salary of not less than twenty-four hundred dollars ($2,400)
limits: No school or college or any other part of the Public School System shall be, directly or indirectly, transferred from the Public School System

a9-s6½.title: School districts in more than one county
a9-s6½.plain: The Constitution does not forbid school districts lying in more than one county, or their issuing bonds under general laws. Officers named in those laws may levy taxes to pay the bonds, which are subject to section eighteen of article eleven.
powers: shall be authorized to levy and assess such taxes and perform all such other acts

a9-s7.title: State and county boards of education
a9-s7.plain: The Legislature shall provide for appointing or electing the State Board of Education and a board of education in each county, or for electing a joint county board of education for two or more counties.

a9-s7.5.title: Textbooks for grades one through eight
a9-s7.5.plain: The State Board of Education shall adopt textbooks for grades one through eight throughout the State, to be furnished without cost as provided by statute.

a9-s8.title: No public money for sectarian schools
a9-s8.plain: No public money may ever be appropriated to support any sectarian or denominational school, or any school not under the exclusive control of public school officers. No sectarian or denominational doctrine may be taught, or instruction on it permitted, in the common schools.
limits: No public money shall ever be appropriated for the support of any sectarian or denominational school
nor shall any sectarian or denominational doctrine be taught

a9-s9.title: University of California and its Regents
a9-s9.plain: The University of California is a public trust administered by the Regents, with full powers of organization and government subject only to limited legislative control. The section sets the board's membership, terms and selection, its property powers, open meetings, and nondiscrimination in admission.
powers: with full powers of organization and government
18 appointive members appointed by the Governor and approved by the Senate
who shall be appointed by the Governor and approved by the Senate
appoint to the board either or both of the following persons as members with all rights of participation
shall be vested with the legal title and the management and disposition of the property of the university
shall have the power to take and hold
shall also have all the powers necessary or convenient for the effective administration of its trust
limits: subject only to such legislative control
no such appointments shall be made
may not be regents of the university at the time of their service on the advisory committee
shall be entirely independent of all political or sectarian influence
no person shall be debarred admission to any department of the university on account of race, religion, ethnic heritage, or sex

a9-s14.title: School district organization
a9-s14.plain: The Legislature has power, by general law, to provide for incorporating and organizing school, high school, and community college districts, and may classify them. It may authorize school district boards to carry on any programs or activities not in conflict with the laws and purposes of school districts.
powers: shall have power, by general law, to provide for the incorporation and organization of school districts, high school districts, and community college districts
may classify such districts
The Legislature may authorize the governing boards of all school districts to initiate and carry on any programs, activities

a9-s16.title: City charters and boards of education
a9-s16.plain: City charters may provide how, when and for what terms members of boards of education are elected or appointed, and for their qualifications, pay, removal and number. Where a district extends beyond the city, changes need approval of the district's voters.
powers: It shall be competent, in all charters framed under the authority given by Section 5 of Article XI, to provide
limits: no charter amendment effecting a change in the manner in which, the times at which, or the terms for which the members of the board of education shall be elected or appointed

a10-s1.title: Eminent domain over navigable water frontages
a10-s1.plain: The right of eminent domain is declared to exist in the State to all frontages on the navigable waters of this State.
powers: The right of eminent domain is hereby declared to exist in the State

a10-s2.title: Reasonable and beneficial use of water
a10-s2.plain: Water must be put to beneficial use to the fullest extent possible and waste prevented. Any right to water is limited to what is reasonably required for the beneficial use served, without depriving riparian owners or appropriators of what they are entitled to. The section is self-executing.
rights: the reasonable use of water of the stream to which the owner’s land is riparian under reasonable methods of diversion and use
powers: the Legislature may also enact laws in the furtherance of the policy in this section contained
limits: is and shall be limited to such water as shall be reasonably required for the beneficial use to be served
does not and shall not extend to the waste or unreasonable use or unreasonable method of use or unreasonable method of diversion of water

a10-s3.title: Tidelands near cities withheld from sale
a10-s3.plain: Tidelands within two miles of any incorporated city, city and county, or town and fronting on navigable harbors, estuaries, bays or inlets shall be withheld from grant or sale to private persons, partnerships or corporations, except certain tidelands reserved solely for street purposes.
powers: may be sold to any town, city, county, city and county, municipal corporations, private persons, partnerships or corporations
limits: shall be withheld from grant or sale to private persons, partnerships, or corporations

a10-s4.title: Public access to navigable waters
a10-s4.plain: No individual, partnership or corporation holding frontage or tidal lands on navigable water may exclude the right of way to that water when required for a public purpose, or obstruct free navigation. The Legislature shall enact laws so access stays always attainable for the people.
rights: access to the navigable waters of this State shall be always attainable for the people thereof
limits: shall be permitted to exclude the right of way to such water
nor to destroy or obstruct the free navigation of such water

a10-s5.title: Water for sale is a public use
a10-s5.plain: The use of water appropriated for sale, rental or distribution is declared a public use, subject to the regulation and control of the State in the manner prescribed by law.
powers: subject to the regulation and control of the State

a10-s6.title: Collecting water rates is a franchise
a10-s6.plain: The right to collect rates or compensation for water supplied to any county, city and county, or town, or their inhabitants, is a franchise and cannot be exercised except by authority of and in the manner prescribed by law.
limits: cannot be exercised except by authority of and in the manner prescribed by law

a10-s7.title: Government land acquisitions follow state water law
a10-s7.plain: When any local, state or federal government agency acquires an interest in real property in California, accepting the interest is an agreement by the agency to conform to California laws on the acquisition, control, use and distribution of water for that land.

a10a-s1.title: Purpose of water protections
a10a-s1.plain: The people of the State provide the guarantees and protections in this article for water rights, water quality, and fish and wildlife resources.

a10a-s2.title: Changes to Senate Bill 200 water protections
a10a-s2.plain: No statute changing the Senate Bill No. 200 provisions on protecting Delta fish and wildlife, existing Delta water rights, and water quality compliance takes effect unless approved by the electors, except a two-thirds legislative statute that does not reduce protection of the delta or fish and wildlife.
powers: amend or repeal, or add to, these provisions
limits: shall become effective unless approved by the electors

a10a-s3.title: No export from wild and scenic rivers
a10a-s3.plain: No water from any component of the California Wild and Scenic Rivers System, as it existed on January 1, 1981, may be appropriated for export into another major hydrologic basin unless expressly authorized first by an initiative statute or a two-thirds vote of each house.
limits: No water shall be available for appropriation by storage in, or by direct diversion from, any of the components of the California Wild and Scenic Rivers System

a10a-s4.title: Changes to the Delta Protection Act
a10a-s4.plain: No statute changing the Delta Protection Act in the Water Code takes effect unless approved by the electors, except a statute passed by two-thirds of each house that does not reduce the protection of the delta or fish and wildlife.
powers: amend or repeal, or add to, these provisions
limits: shall become effective unless approved by the electors

a10a-s5.title: No eminent domain over Delta water rights for export
a10a-s5.plain: No public agency may use eminent domain to acquire Delta water rights or Delta water contract rights in order to export the water. Eminent domain may still be used to acquire land or other rights needed to build water facilities.
limits: No public agency may utilize eminent domain proceedings to acquire water rights

a10a-s6.title: Venue and speedy handling of water lawsuits
a10a-s6.plain: Listed lawsuits over Senate Bill No. 200, the peripheral canal and related water agreements must be brought in Sacramento County within set time limits, get preference and prompt hearings, and may be transferred to the Supreme Court on any party's request.
powers: may apply to the State Board of Control for actual costs imposed by the requirements of this section upon the county
exercising the transfer authority contained in Article VI, Section 12 of the Constitution

a10a-s7.title: State agencies must honor water protections
a10a-s7.plain: State agencies shall exercise their authorized powers in a manner consistent with the protections provided by this article.

a10a-s8.title: Article depends on Senate Bill 200
a10a-s8.plain: This article has no force or effect unless Senate Bill No. 200 of the 1979–80 Regular Session of the Legislature is enacted and takes effect.

a10b-s1.title: Name of the article
a10b-s1.plain: This article may be cited as the Marine Resources Protection Act of 1990.

a10b-s2.title: Definitions for marine resources protection
a10b-s2.plain: Defines "District", "Ocean waters" and the Marine Resources Protection "Zone" (waters around the Channel Islands and near the southern mainland coast), and says Fish and Game Code references mean the statutes in effect on January 1, 1990.

a10b-s3.title: Gill and trammel nets banned in the zone
