a10b-s3.plain: From 1991 through 1993, gill nets or trammel nets may be used in the zone only under a nontransferable Department of Fish and Game permit. On and after January 1, 1994, they shall not be used in the zone.
limits: may only be used in the zone pursuant to a nontransferable permit
shall not be used in the zone

a10b-s4.title: Gill net limits for rockfish and northern waters
a10b-s4.plain: Gill and trammel nets may not be used to take any rockfish. North of Point Arguello, their use is governed by the Fish and Game Code provisions in effect in 1990 or 1989. The Legislature may add restrictions; the Director may not authorize use where it is not permitted.
powers: imposing more restrictions on the use and/or possession of gill nets or trammel nets
limits: may not be used to take any species of rockfish
shall not authorize the use of gill nets or trammel nets in any area where the use is not permitted

a10b-s5.title: Gill net permits during the phase-out
a10b-s5.plain: For 1991 through 1993, the Department of Fish and Game shall issue a gill net or trammel net permit for the zone to any applicant with a commercial fishing license and a Section 8681 permit who owns or operates a vessel equipped with such a net.

a10b-s6.title: Gill net permit fees
a10b-s6.plain: The Department of Fish and Game shall charge fees for Section 5 permits of $250 in 1991, 500 in 1992, and 1,000 in 1993.

a10b-s7.title: Compensation for giving up gill net permits
a10b-s7.plain: Permit holders who timely notified the Department of Fish and Game could surrender their permits and stop gill or trammel net fishing in the zone for a one time compensation based on past landings, subject to verification, appeal, and enabling legislation by July 1, 1993.
rights: a one time compensation
may appeal that decision to the Fish and Game Commission
limits: shall not be compensated pursuant to subdivision (b)
no compensation shall be paid under this article

a10b-s8.title: Marine Resources Protection Account and stamps
a10b-s8.plain: Creates the Marine Resources Protection Account; the Department of Fish and Game collects fees under this article for compensating permit holders and administration. Sport and commercial passenger fishing south of Point Arguello require a $3 stamp. This section becomes inoperative January 1, 1995.
powers: may be expended for the administration of this article
may accept contributions or donations from any person
limits: shall be used only for those purposes
may only be expended for the purposes authorized by this article

a10b-s9.title: Leftover account funds for marine research
a10b-s9.plain: Funds remaining in the Marine Resources Protection Account on or after January 1, 1995, shall, with the Fish and Game Commission's approval, be used for grants to colleges, universities and other scientific research groups for marine research within the ecological reserves.

a10b-s10.title: Annual report to the Legislature
a10b-s10.plain: By December 31 each year, the Director of Fish and Game shall prepare and submit a report to the Legislature on carrying out this article, including an accounting of all funds.

a10b-s11.title: No dealing in illegally taken fish
a10b-s11.plain: It is unlawful for any person to take, possess, receive, transport, purchase, sell, barter or process any fish obtained in violation of this article.
limits: unlawful for any person to take, possess, receive, transport, purchase, sell, barter, or process any fish obtained in violation of this article

a10b-s12.title: Monitoring commercial fish landings
a10b-s12.plain: To increase scientific information on ocean fisheries, the Department of Fish and Game shall set up a program to monitor and evaluate daily landings by permitted commercial fishermen. The commercial fishing industry shall bear the cost.

a10b-s13.title: Penalties for marine net violations
a10b-s13.plain: Violating Sections 3 and 4 brings a fine and mandatory suspension of commercial fishing licenses, permits or stamps, larger for repeat violations. A Section 8 violation is treated as a Fish and Game Code violation. Probation must require paying at least the minimum fine.

a10b-s14.title: Four new ocean ecological reserves
a10b-s14.plain: Before January 1, 1994, the Fish and Game Commission shall establish four new ecological reserves of at least two square miles each in ocean waters along the mainland coast, and restrict their use to scientific research on managing and enhancing marine resources.

a10b-s15.title: Other wildlife closures not preempted
a10b-s15.plain: This article does not preempt or supersede any other closures to protect any other wildlife, including sea otters, whales and shorebirds.

a10b-s16.title: Severability of the article
a10b-s16.plain: If any provision of this article or its application is held invalid, the invalidity does not affect other provisions or applications that can be given effect without it; the provisions of this article are severable.

a11-s1.title: Counties
a11-s1.plain: The State is divided into counties. The Legislature shall prescribe procedure for county formation, consolidation and boundary changes, and provide for county powers and elected county officers. A county seat may be removed only by a two-thirds vote of the county's electors.
powers: may provide for other officers
limits: No county seat shall be removed
shall not be submitted in the same county more than once in four years

a11-s2.title: Cities
a11-s2.plain: The Legislature shall prescribe uniform procedure for forming cities and provide for city powers. A city may not be annexed to or consolidated into another without approval by a majority of its electors voting on the question.
limits: a city may not be annexed to or consolidated into another

a11-s3.title: County and city charters
a11-s3.plain: A county or city may adopt a charter for its own government by majority vote of its electors. A charter takes effect when filed with the Secretary of State and has the force of legislative enactments. Charters may be proposed, amended or repealed by the governing body or by initiative.
powers: may adopt a charter
may propose a charter or revision
may be proposed by initiative or by the governing body
may be required by initiative or by the governing body

a11-s4.title: What county charters must provide
a11-s4.plain: County charters shall provide for an elected governing body of 5 or more members, elected county officers, compensation, terms and removal, county functions, officers' powers and duties, and employees. Charters supersede general laws on those matters, and charter counties have all powers provided for counties.
powers: shall have all the powers that are provided by this Constitution or by statute for counties

a11-s5.title: City charters and municipal affairs
a11-s5.plain: A city charter may provide that the city may make and enforce all ordinances and regulations on municipal affairs, subject only to its charter; on other matters cities are subject to general laws. City charters supersede inconsistent laws on municipal affairs and may provide for police, subgovernment, elections and municipal officers and employees.
powers: may make and enforce all ordinances and regulations in respect to municipal affairs
It shall be competent in all city charters to provide
plenary authority is hereby granted

a11-s6.title: Consolidated charter city and county
a11-s6.plain: A county and all cities within it may consolidate as a charter city and county as provided by statute. A charter city and county is both a charter city and a charter county, and its charter city powers supersede conflicting charter county powers.
powers: may consolidate as a charter city and county

a11-s7.title: Local ordinances and regulations
a11-s7.plain: A county or city may make and enforce within its limits all local, police, sanitary and other ordinances and regulations not in conflict with general laws.
powers: may make and enforce within its limits all local, police, sanitary, and other ordinances and regulations

a11-s7.5.title: Limits on local ballot measures
a11-s7.5.plain: A city or county measure proposed by a local legislative body and submitted to voters may not include or exclude areas based on the vote, or contain alternative provisions that take effect depending on the percentage of votes cast. The section defines "city or county measure."
limits: may not do either of the following

a11-s8.title: Counties performing city functions
a11-s8.plain: The Legislature may provide that counties perform municipal functions at the request of cities within them. If their charters provide, a county may agree with a city within it to assume and discharge specified municipal functions.
powers: may provide that counties perform municipal functions
may agree with a city within it to assume and discharge specified municipal functions

a11-s9.title: Municipal public utilities
a11-s9.plain: A municipal corporation may establish, purchase and operate public works furnishing light, water, power, heat, transportation or communication, and may serve outside its boundaries except within another municipal corporation that furnishes the same service and does not consent. Persons or corporations may operate such works under city regulations.
powers: may establish, purchase, and operate public works
may furnish those services outside its boundaries
may establish and operate works for supplying those services

a11-s10.title: Extra pay and residency limits for local employees
a11-s10.plain: A local government body may not grant extra compensation or allowance after service is rendered or a contract performed, or pay a claim under an agreement made without authority of law. Cities, counties and public districts may not require employees to be residents, but may require them to live within a reasonable and specific distance.
limits: may not grant extra compensation or extra allowance
pay a claim under an agreement made without authority of law
may not require that its employees be residents of such city, county, or district

a11-s11.title: No delegation of local powers to private bodies
a11-s11.plain: The Legislature may not delegate to a private person or body power over county or municipal improvements, money, or property, to levy taxes or assessments, or to perform municipal functions. It may provide for deposit and investment of public moneys and for bond payment and registration.
powers: may, however, provide for the deposit of public moneys
may also provide for investment of public moneys in securities
limits: may not delegate to a private person or body power

a11-s12.title: Claims against counties and cities
a11-s12.plain: The Legislature may prescribe procedure for presenting, considering, and enforcing claims against counties, cities, and their officers, agents, or employees.
powers: may prescribe procedure for presentation, consideration, and enforcement of claims

a11-s13.title: Article XI restates earlier provisions
a11-s13.plain: Sections 1(b) (except its second sentence), 3(a), 4, and 5 of Article XI, on powers between the Legislature and cities and counties, restate the earlier Constitution with no substantive change. "General law," "general laws," and "laws" continue their earlier meaning.

a11-s14.title: Voter approval for multi-county property taxes
a11-s14.plain: A local government formed after this section took effect, whose boundaries include all or part of two or more counties, may not levy a property tax unless a majority of its qualified voters voting on the tax approve it.
limits: shall not levy a property tax

a11-s15.title: Vehicle license fee revenues for local governments
a11-s15.plain: Vehicle license fee revenues from the rate up to 0.65 percent of a vehicle's market value go to the Local Revenue Fund and to cities and counties. If the Legislature lowers the fee below that, it must provide an equal replacement amount for them.

a12-s1.title: Public Utilities Commission members
a12-s1.plain: The Public Utilities Commission has 5 members appointed by the Governor and approved by a Senate majority, for staggered 6-year terms. The Legislature may remove a member for incompetence, neglect of duty, or corruption by a two-thirds vote of each house.
powers: The Legislature may remove a member for incompetence, neglect of duty, or corruption

a12-s2.title: Commission procedures and hearings
a12-s2.plain: Subject to statute and due process, the commission may set its own procedures. A commissioner designated by the commission may hold a hearing or investigation or issue an order, subject to commission approval.
powers: the commission may establish its own procedures
may hold a hearing or investigation or issue an order

a12-s3.title: What are public utilities
a12-s3.plain: Private corporations and persons that run transportation, telephone and telegraph, or heat, light, water, power, storage, or wharfage systems for the public, and common carriers, are public utilities subject to control by the Legislature, which may add further classes.
powers: are public utilities subject to control by the Legislature
may prescribe that additional classes of private corporations or other persons are public utilities

a12-s4.title: Transportation rates and charges
a12-s4.plain: The commission may fix rates and rules for transportation companies, prohibit discrimination, and award reparation for unreasonable charges. A transportation company may not raise a rate without a commission decision that it is justified, reviewable only as to confiscation.
powers: The commission may fix rates and establish rules for the transportation of passengers and property
prohibit discrimination
award reparation for the exaction of unreasonable, excessive, or discriminatory charges
limits: A transportation company may not raise a rate or incidental charge
shall not be subject to judicial review

a12-s5.title: Legislature's plenary power over the commission
a12-s5.plain: The Legislature has plenary power, unlimited by the rest of the constitution but consistent with this article, to give the commission more authority and jurisdiction, set how courts review its actions, and enable it to fix just compensation for utility property taken by eminent domain.
powers: The Legislature has plenary power
to confer additional authority and jurisdiction upon the commission
to establish the manner and scope of review of commission action in a court of record
to enable it to fix just compensation for utility property taken by eminent domain

a12-s6.title: Commission powers over public utilities
a12-s6.plain: The commission may fix rates, establish rules, examine records, issue subpenas, administer oaths, take testimony, punish for contempt, and prescribe a uniform system of accounts for all public utilities subject to its jurisdiction.
powers: The commission may fix rates, establish rules, examine records, issue subpenas, administer oaths, take testimony, punish for contempt
prescribe a uniform system of accounts

a12-s7.title: Free passes and commissioner conflicts
a12-s7.plain: A transportation company may not give free passes or discounts to state officeholders; a public officer, other than a Public Utilities Commissioner, who accepts one forfeits the office. A commissioner may not hold an official relation to or financial interest in anyone the commission regulates.
limits: A transportation company may not grant free passes or discounts to anyone holding an office in this State
shall work a forfeiture of that office
may not hold an official relation to nor have a financial interest in a person or corporation subject to regulation by the commission

a12-s8.title: Local regulation of commission matters
a12-s8.plain: A city, county, or other public body may not regulate matters over which the Legislature gives the Commission regulatory power. This does not affect certain powers under city charters existing on October 10, 1911, or any city's right to grant franchises as prescribed by law.
limits: may not regulate matters over which the Legislature grants regulatory power to the Commission

a12-s9.title: Article XII restates earlier provisions
a12-s9.plain: The provisions of this article restate all related provisions of the earlier Constitution and make no substantive change.

a13-s1.title: All property taxable at uniform value
a13-s1.plain: Unless this Constitution or federal law provides otherwise, all property is taxable, assessed at the same percentage of fair market value, and taxed in proportion to its full value.

a13-s2.title: Taxation of personal property
a13-s2.plain: The Legislature may provide for property taxation of tangible personal property, stock, evidences of indebtedness, and interests in them, and by two-thirds vote may classify such property for differential taxation or exemption. Taxes on notes, stock, bonds, and similar interests may not exceed 0.4 percent of full value.
powers: may provide for property taxation of all forms of tangible personal property
may classify such personal property for differential taxation or for exemption
limits: shall not exceed four-tenths of one percent of full value
shall not be higher on personal property than on real property in the same taxing jurisdiction

a13-s3.title: Property exempt from taxation
a13-s3.plain: Lists property exempt from property taxation, including state and local government property, public bonds, schools, libraries, religious worship, cemeteries, growing crops, young trees, a $7,000 homeowners' exemption, ships, household goods, debts secured by land, and $1,000 for certain veterans and their families.
powers: The Legislature may supersede the foregoing provisions with an alternative system or systems of taxing or exempting forest trees or timber
The Legislature may increase this exemption and may deny it
limits: are exempt from property taxation
This property is also exempt from special assessment
is ineligible for this exemption
shall lose eligibility for the exemption

a13-s3.5.title: Adjusting veterans' exemption values
a13-s3.5.plain: In any year the assessment ratio changes, the Legislature must adjust the valuation of property described in subdivisions (o), (p) and (q) of Section 3 to keep the same proportionate values.

a13-s4.title: Exemptions the Legislature may grant
a13-s4.plain: The Legislature may exempt from property taxation, wholly or partly, the homes of certain disabled or deceased veterans and their spouses, nonprofit religious, hospital, or charitable property, property of certain named institutions, and parking for places of worship.
powers: The Legislature may exempt from property taxation in whole or in part

a13-s5.title: Exemptions cover property under construction
a13-s5.plain: Exemptions under Sections 3(e), 3(f), and 4(b) apply to buildings under construction, land required for their convenient use, and equipment in them, if the intended use would qualify the property for exemption.

a13-s6.title: Failure to claim a property tax exemption
a13-s6.plain: Failing in any year to claim, in the manner required by law at the time, an exemption or classification that reduces a property tax is deemed a waiver of it for that year.

a13-s7.title: Exempting low-value real property
a13-s7.plain: With two-thirds of each house concurring, the Legislature may authorize county boards of supervisors to exempt real property worth so little that its taxes and subventions would be less than the cost of assessing and collecting them.
powers: may authorize county boards of supervisors to exempt real property

a13-s8.title: Open space and historical property valuation
a13-s8.plain: The Legislature may define open space land and property of historical significance, and must provide that when such land or property is enforceably restricted, it is valued for property tax purposes only on a basis consistent with its restrictions and uses.
powers: may define open space land
may define such property

a13-s8.5.title: Property tax postponement for seniors and disabled
a13-s8.5.plain: The Legislature may provide for low or moderate income persons 62 or older, and disabled persons, to postpone property taxes on their principal residence, and must provide subventions to local governments for the revenue lost.
powers: may provide by law for the manner in which a person of low or moderate income
may also provide by law for the manner in which a disabled person
shall have plenary power to define all terms in this section

a13-s9.title: Assessing single-family homes by use
a13-s9.plain: The Legislature may provide for assessing an owner-occupied single-family dwelling, and the land needed for its use, only on the basis of use, when it is on land zoned exclusively for single-family dwellings or agriculture.
powers: may provide for the assessment for taxation only on the basis of use of a single-family dwelling

a13-s10.title: Assessment of nonprofit golf courses
a13-s10.plain: Real property of 10 or more acres used only for nonprofit golf course purposes for at least 2 years before the lien date is assessed on the basis of that use, plus any value from minerals or hydrocarbons.

a13-s11.title: Taxing local government land outside its boundaries
a13-s11.plain: Land, water rights and improvements a local government owns outside its boundaries are taxable in stated cases, chiefly in Inyo and Mono Counties, under set assessment formulas. Water-based levies between local governments are barred, and the State Board of Equalization may review these assessments.
powers: shall be subject to review, equalization, and adjustment by the State Board of Equalization
limits: shall not diminish the quantity of water rights assessable and taxable
the assessed value shall not exceed the product of
No tax, charge, assessment, or levy of any character
shall not exceed the value of all interests in the land

a13-s12.title: Tax rates on unsecured property
a13-s12.plain: Taxes on personal property, possessory interests, and improvements on exempt land that are not secured by a lien on land are levied at the prior year's secured rates; the Legislature must adjust that rate when the assessment ratio changes.

a13-s13.title: Separate assessment of land and improvements
a13-s13.plain: Land and improvements must be assessed separately.

a13-s14.title: Where local property is assessed
a13-s14.plain: All property taxed by local government must be assessed in the county, city, and district where it is located.

a13-s15.title: Reassessing damaged or destroyed property
a13-s15.plain: The Legislature may authorize local government to provide for assessing or reassessing taxable property physically damaged or destroyed after the lien date.
powers: may authorize local government to provide for the assessment or reassessment of taxable property

a13-s16.title: County boards of equalization
a13-s16.plain: The county board of supervisors, or assessment appeals boards it creates, is the county board of equalization, which equalizes values on the local assessment roll. Supervisors support those boards, and the Legislature provides for their members and joint creation.
powers: may jointly create one or more assessment appeals boards
may provide for their discontinuance

a13-s17.title: State Board of Equalization membership
a13-s17.plain: The Board of Equalization has 5 voting members: the Controller and 4 members elected from four districts for 4-year terms at gubernatorial elections. No member may serve more than 2 terms.
limits: No member may serve more than 2 terms

a13-s18.title: Equalizing county assessment levels
a13-s18.plain: The Board must measure county assessment levels each year and bring them into conformity by adjusting entire secured local rolls. If the State levies a property tax, remaining unequal levels are corrected for distributing that tax.

a13-s19.title: State assessment of utility property
a13-s19.plain: The Board must assess each year multi-county pipelines, canals and aqueducts and the property of regulated railway, telegraph, telephone, gas and electric companies. Those companies may not face differing taxes or license charges; the Board may delegate some assessment to local assessors.
powers: may authorize Board assessment of property owned or used by other public utilities
may delegate to a local assessor the duty to assess a property
limits: No other tax or license charge may be imposed on these companies

a13-s20.title: Local tax rate and bonding limits
a13-s20.plain: The Legislature may provide maximum property tax rates and bonding limits for local governments.
powers: may provide maximum property tax rates and bonding limits for local governments

a13-s21.title: School district tax levies
a13-s21.plain: Within any limits under Section 20, the Legislature must provide for county governing bodies to levy each year school district taxes sufficient to produce the revenues each district’s board determines its schools and functions require.

a13-s22.title: Cap on state property tax revenue
a13-s22.plain: Not more than 25 percent of the State's total appropriations from all funds may be raised by taxes on real and personal property according to its value.
limits: Not more than 25 percent of the total appropriations from all funds of the State

a13-s23.title: Taxing property after boundary changes
a13-s23.plain: If the state's boundaries change, the Legislature must determine how the affected property is taxed.

a13-s24.title: Local taxes and local tax proceeds
a13-s24.plain: The Legislature may not impose taxes for local purposes but may authorize local governments to impose them, and may not take or redirect proceeds of local taxes levied solely for local purposes. State money given to local governments may be used as provided.
powers: may authorize local governments to impose them
limits: may not impose taxes for local purposes
may not reallocate, transfer, borrow, appropriate, restrict the use of, or otherwise use the proceeds

a13-s25.title: Reimbursing local revenue lost under Section 3(k)
a13-s25.plain: The Legislature must reimburse each local government, in the same fiscal year, for revenue lost because of Section 3(k).

a13-s25.5.title: Protecting local tax revenues from state statutes
a13-s25.5.plain: On or after November 3, 2004, the Legislature may not enact statutes that reduce local shares of property tax, restrict local sales and transactions taxes, or take redevelopment agency taxes, except as allowed here; it may change some use tax distributions and authorize revenue exchanges.
powers: The Legislature may change by statute the method of distributing the revenues
The Legislature may authorize by statute two or more specifically identified local agencies
limits: the Legislature shall not enact a statute to do any of the following
shall not result in a total ad valorem property tax revenue loss
The Legislature shall not change the pro rata shares of ad valorem property tax

a13-s26.title: Income taxes and income tax exemptions
a13-s26.plain: Taxes on or measured by income may be imposed as prescribed by law. Interest on state and local government bonds, certain income of nonprofit colleges, and certain nonprofit organizations are exempt from the taxes described.
powers: Taxes on or measured by income may be imposed
limits: is exempt from taxes on income
is exempt from taxes on or measured by income
is exempt from any business license tax or fee measured by income or gross receipts

a13-s27.title: Taxing corporations and banks
a13-s27.plain: By a majority of each house, the Legislature may tax corporations, including banks, and their franchises by any method not prohibited. Unless the Legislature provides otherwise, the bank tax is measured by net income and replaces other taxes and fees on banks, with exceptions.
powers: may tax corporations, including state and national banks, and their franchises

a13-s28.title: Tax on insurers
a13-s28.plain: Imposes an annual 2.35 percent tax on insurers doing business in California, measured by premiums or, for title insurers, income, in lieu of most other taxes, with retaliatory taxes on out-of-state insurers and a separate ocean marine tax. The Legislature may change the rates.
powers: may by law change the rate or rates of taxes herein imposed upon insurers

a13-s29.title: Local sales tax sharing contracts
a13-s29.plain: The Legislature may authorize counties and cities to contract to share sales or use tax revenue, with voter approval in each jurisdiction. They may also contract to share Bradley-Burns sales and use tax revenue if two-thirds of each governing body approves.
powers: may authorize counties, cities and counties, and cities to enter into contracts
may enter into contracts to apportion between them the revenue

a13-s30.title: Old tax liens presumed paid
a13-s30.plain: A tax is conclusively presumed paid 30 years after it became a lien, unless the property has been sold for the tax in the manner the Legislature provides.

a13-s31.title: Power to tax cannot be surrendered
a13-s31.plain: The power to tax may not be surrendered or suspended by grant or contract.
limits: may not be surrendered or suspended by grant or contract

a13-s32.title: No court orders stopping tax collection
a13-s32.plain: No court process may issue against the State or its officers to prevent or enjoin collecting a tax. After paying a tax claimed to be illegal, a taxpayer may sue to recover it with interest as the Legislature provides.
rights: an action may be maintained to recover the tax paid, with interest
limits: No legal or equitable process shall issue

a13-s33.title: Legislature to carry out the taxation article
a13-s33.plain: The Legislature must pass all laws necessary to carry out this article.

a13-s34.title: No sales tax on food
a13-s34.plain: Neither the State nor its political subdivisions may levy or collect a sales or use tax on food products for human consumption, except as provided by statute as of the effective date of this section.
limits: Neither the State of California nor any of its political subdivisions shall levy or collect a sales or use tax

a13-s35.title: Sales tax for local public safety
a13-s35.plain: Imposes an added one-half percent sales and use tax from January 1, 1994, whose revenues go to the Local Public Safety Fund for counties that request or approve it, to be used exclusively for local public safety services.

a13-s36.title: Public safety realignment and Education Protection Account
a13-s36.plain: Dedicates certain tax and fee revenues to local Public Safety Services under the 2011 Realignment Legislation, limits new unfunded costs on local agencies, creates the Education Protection Account funded by temporary tax increases, and sets how its money is estimated, transferred, spent and audited.
rights: an appropriate party may seek judicial relief
powers: shall have sole authority to determine how the moneys received from the Education Protection Account are spent
may perform audits of expenditures from the Local Revenue Fund 2011
may seek civil or criminal penalties
limits: 2011 Realignment Legislation shall include no new programs assigned to local agencies after January 1, 2012
The State shall not submit to the federal government any plans or waivers
shall not be used by local agencies to supplant other funding for Public Safety Services
shall not be used to pay any costs incurred by the Legislature, the Governor, or any agency of state government

a13a-s1.title: One percent cap on property tax
a13a-s1.plain: Ad valorem tax on real property may not exceed 1 percent of full cash value, except for taxes to pay certain voter-approved debts, including school bonds approved by 55 percent of voters that meet listed accountability requirements.
powers: may levy a 55 percent vote ad valorem tax
limits: shall not exceed One percent (1%) of the full cash value of such property

a13a-s2.title: Full cash value and reassessment of real property
a13a-s2.plain: Defines full cash value as the 1975–76 assessed value or the value when later purchased, newly constructed or changed in ownership, allows yearly increases up to 2 percent, and lets or requires the Legislature to provide exclusions and base year value transfers for listed situations.
powers: the Legislature may provide that, under appropriate circumstances
the Legislature may authorize each county board of supervisors, after consultation
The Legislature may extend the provisions of this subdivision
the Legislature may provide that the term
the Legislature may authorize each county board of supervisors to adopt
limits: shall not exceed the scope and amount of the benefit
the owner shall not receive the relief

a13a-s2.1.title: Moving and inheriting taxable value of homes
a13a-s2.1.plain: From April 1, 2021, owners over 55, severely disabled, or wildfire or disaster victims may transfer their home's taxable value to a replacement home anywhere in the state. From February 16, 2021, parent-child and some grandparent transfers of a family home or farm keep its taxable value up to a limit.
rights: may transfer the taxable value of their primary residence to a replacement primary residence located anywhere in this state
shall be entitled to a refund of taxes previously owed or paid
limits: shall not be allowed to transfer the taxable value of a primary residence more than three times

a13a-s2.2.title: Fire response and county revenue funds
a13a-s2.2.plain: Creates the California Fire Response Fund and County Revenue Protection Fund. The Director of Finance calculates the state's yearly gains from Section 2.1, the Controller transfers 75 and 15 percent of them to those funds, and fire fund money goes to expand fire suppression staffing.
limits: shall not be appropriated for any other purpose
the Controller shall not transfer the amount in excess of that 10 percent

a13a-s2.3.title: Reimbursing local agencies for Section 2.1 losses
a13a-s2.3.plain: Each county determines yearly the revenue gain or loss for itself and its local agencies from Section 2.1. Those with a negative gain are reimbursed every three years by the California Department of Tax and Fee Administration from the County Revenue Protection Fund.

a13a-s3.title: Two-thirds vote for state tax increases
a13a-s3.plain: A change in state statute that makes any taxpayer pay a higher tax must pass by two-thirds of all members of each house, and no new ad valorem taxes on real property or taxes on its sale may be imposed. The State bears the burden of proof.
limits: must be imposed by an act passed by not less than two-thirds of all members elected to each of the two houses of the Legislature
no new ad valorem taxes on real property, or sales or transaction taxes on the sales of real property may be imposed

a13a-s4.title: Local special taxes by two-thirds vote
a13a-s4.plain: Cities, counties and special districts may impose special taxes by a two-thirds vote of their qualified electors, except ad valorem taxes on real property or transaction or sales taxes on the sale of real property.
powers: may impose special taxes on such district

a13a-s5.title: When the tax limitation article takes effect
a13a-s5.plain: This article takes effect for the tax year beginning on July 1 following its passage, except Section 3, which becomes effective upon the passage of the article.

a13a-s6.title: Severability of the tax limitation article
a13a-s6.plain: If any section, part, clause or phrase of this article is held invalid or unconstitutional, the remaining sections are not affected and remain in full force and effect.

a13a-s7.title: Children and Families First Act exempt from Section 3
a13a-s7.plain: Section 3 of this article, on the vote needed for state tax increases, does not apply to the California Children and Families First Act of 1998.

a13b-s1.title: Annual appropriations limit
a13b-s1.plain: The total annual appropriations subject to limitation of the State and of each local government may not exceed its limit for the prior year, adjusted for changes in the cost of living and population, except as this article otherwise provides.
limits: shall not exceed the appropriations limit of the entity of government for the prior year

a13b-s1.5.title: Audit of local appropriations limits
a13b-s1.5.plain: Each local government's annual calculation of its appropriations limit must be reviewed as part of an annual financial audit.

a13b-s2.title: Returning excess revenues
a13b-s2.plain: State revenues over two years above what may be appropriated under this article are split: half is transferred under Section 8.5 of Article XVI and half returned by revising tax rates or fees. Other entities return all such excess revenues.

a13b-s3.title: Adjusting the appropriations limit
a13b-s3.plain: The appropriations limit is adjusted when responsibility for services moves between governments or to private entities or fees, and may be exceeded in a declared emergency if later limits are reduced. Emergency appropriations approved by two-thirds after a Governor's declaration are not subject to limitation.

a13b-s4.title: Voters may change an appropriations limit
a13b-s4.plain: The electors of an entity of government may establish or change its appropriations limit, following constitutional and statutory voting requirements. Such a change lasts as the electors decide, but never more than four years from their most recent vote.
powers: may be established or changed by the electors of such entity
limits: shall in no event exceed four years from the most recent vote of said electors

a13b-s5.title: Contingency, reserve and similar funds
a13b-s5.plain: Each entity of government may set up reserve and similar funds it deems reasonable and proper. Contributions from tax proceeds count as appropriations subject to limitation; withdrawals, their spending, and transfers between funds do not.
powers: may establish such contingency, emergency, unemployment, reserve, retirement, sinking fund, trust, or similar funds

a13b-s5.5.title: Prudent state reserve fund
a13b-s5.5.plain: The Legislature must establish a prudent state reserve fund in the amount it deems reasonable and necessary. Contributions to and withdrawals from the fund are subject to Section 5 of this article.

a13b-s6.title: State reimbursement for local mandates
a13b-s6.plain: When the Legislature or a state agency mandates a new program or higher level of service on local government, the State must reimburse the costs, with listed exceptions. The Legislature must pay or suspend mandates found payable, and property tax revenues may not be used.
powers: the Legislature may, but need not, provide a subvention of funds
limits: Ad valorem property tax revenues shall not be used to reimburse a local government

a13b-s7.title: Bonded debt obligations protected
a13b-s7.plain: Nothing in this article is to be construed to impair the ability of the State or any local government to meet its obligations on existing or future bonded indebtedness.

a13b-s8.title: Definitions for the spending limitation
a13b-s8.plain: Defines terms used in this article, including appropriations subject to limitation, proceeds of taxes, local government, change in the cost of living, change in population, debt service and appropriations limit. Each local entity selects its cost-of-living measure annually by recorded vote.

a13b-s9.title: Appropriations excluded from the limit
a13b-s9.plain: Appropriations subject to limitation do not include appropriations for debt service, court or federal mandates, certain special districts, qualified capital outlay projects, or revenue from certain motor vehicle fuel taxes, related sales and use taxes, and commercial vehicle weight fees.

a13b-s10.title: When the spending limitation takes effect
a13b-s10.plain: This article is effective beginning with the first day of the fiscal year following its adoption.

a13b-s10.5.title: Appropriations limit from 1990 onward
a13b-s10.5.plain: For fiscal years beginning on or after July 1, 1990, each entity's appropriations limit is its 1986–87 limit adjusted for the changes made under this article as amended, and for the changes required by Section 3.

a13b-s11.title: Court judgments and severability
a13b-s11.plain: If a final court judgment adds or removes an appropriation category from those subject to limitation, the appropriations limit is adjusted accordingly. If any part of this article is held invalid, the rest remains in full force.

a13b-s12.title: Tobacco surtax fund outside the limit
a13b-s12.plain: Appropriations of revenue from the Cigarette and Tobacco Products Surtax Fund are not appropriations subject to limitation, and depositing or appropriating that revenue requires no adjustment in any appropriations limit under Section 3.

a13b-s13.title: Children and Families trust fund outside the limit
a13b-s13.plain: Appropriations from the California Children and Families First Trust Fund are not subject to limitation and need no Section 3 adjustment. The Act's surtax is not General Fund revenue for purposes of Section 8 of Article XVI.

a13b-s14.title: 2016 tobacco tax fund outside the limit
a13b-s14.plain: Appropriations of revenue from the California Healthcare, Research and Prevention Tobacco Tax Act of 2016 Fund are not subject to limitation, and depositing or appropriating that revenue requires no adjustment in any appropriations limit under Section 3.

a13b-s15.title: Road repair revenues excluded from spending limit
a13b-s15.plain: Appropriations of revenues from the Road Maintenance and Rehabilitation Account, or other revenues deposited under the Road Repair and Accountability Act of 2017, are not appropriations subject to limitation, and no adjustment of any appropriations limit is required because of them.

a13c-s1.title: Definitions for local tax voter approval
a13c-s1.plain: Defines general tax, local government, special district, special tax and tax for this article, lists seven kinds of charges that are not taxes, and puts on the local government the burden of proving that a levy is not a tax.

a13c-s2.title: Voter approval of local general and special taxes
a13c-s2.plain: Every local tax is either general or special. Special purpose districts may not levy general taxes. A local government may not impose, extend or increase a general tax without majority voter approval, or a special tax without two-thirds voter approval.
limits: shall have no power to levy general taxes
No local government may impose, extend, or increase any general tax
No local government may impose, extend, or increase any special tax

a13c-s3.title: Initiative power over local taxes and fees
a13c-s3.plain: The initiative power may not be prohibited or limited in reducing or repealing any local tax, assessment, fee or charge. It applies to all local governments, and neither the Legislature nor a local charter may require more signatures than for statewide statutory initiatives.
powers: The power of initiative to affect local taxes, assessments, fees and charges shall be applicable to all local governments
limits: the initiative power shall not be prohibited or otherwise limited
neither the Legislature nor any local government charter shall impose a signature requirement higher than that applicable to statewide statutory initiatives

a13d-s1.title: Scope of the assessment and fee article
a13d-s1.plain: This article applies to all assessments, fees and charges, whether imposed under state statute or local charter authority. Nothing in it or in Article XIII C gives any agency new authority to tax, or affects existing laws on development fees or timber yield taxes.

a13d-s2.title: Definitions for assessments and property fees
a13d-s2.plain: Defines the terms used in this article: agency, assessment, capital cost, district, fee or charge, maintenance and operation expenses, property ownership, property-related service and special benefit.

a13d-s3.title: Limits on property taxes, assessments and fees
a13d-s3.plain: No agency may levy a tax, assessment, fee or charge on a parcel or on a person as an incident of property ownership except the ad valorem property tax, a special tax approved by two-thirds vote, and assessments and property-related fees as this article provides.
limits: No tax, assessment, fee, or charge shall be assessed by any agency upon any parcel of property or upon any person as an incident of property ownership

a13d-s4.title: Procedures and requirements for assessments
a13d-s4.plain: An agency proposing an assessment must identify benefited parcels, limit each assessment to the parcel's proportional special benefit, support it with an engineer's report, mail notice and a ballot to owners, and hold a hearing; it may not impose the assessment if there is a majority protest.
limits: No assessment shall be imposed on any parcel which exceeds the reasonable cost of the proportional special benefit conferred on that parcel
shall not be exempt from assessment
The agency shall not impose an assessment if there is a majority protest
the assessment shall not be imposed unless approved by a two-thirds vote of the electorate in the district

a13d-s5.title: Effective date of the assessment and fee article
a13d-s5.plain: This article takes effect the day after the election unless otherwise provided. From July 1, 1997, all assessments must comply with it, but four kinds of existing assessments are exempt from Section 4's procedures, though later increases in three of them are not.

a13d-s6.title: Property-related fees and charges
a13d-s6.plain: An agency must give mailed notice and hold a hearing before imposing or increasing a property-related fee, and may not impose it over a majority written protest. Fees may not exceed the cost of the service or be used for other purposes, and most need voter approval.
powers: An agency may adopt procedures similar to those for increases in assessments
limits: the agency shall not impose the fee or charge
A fee or charge shall not be extended, imposed, or increased by any agency
shall not exceed the funds required to provide the property related service
shall not be used for any purpose other than that for which the fee or charge was imposed
shall not exceed the proportional cost of the service attributable to the parcel
No fee or charge may be imposed for a service unless that service is actually used by, or immediately available to, the owner of the property in question
Fees or charges based on potential or future use of a service are not permitted
No fee or charge may be imposed for general governmental services
no property related fee or charge shall be imposed or increased unless and until that fee or charge is submitted and approved

a14-s1.title: Minimum wages and employee welfare
a14-s1.plain: The Legislature may provide for minimum wages and for the general welfare of employees, and for those purposes may give a commission legislative, executive and judicial powers.
powers: may provide for minimum wages and for the general welfare of employees
may confer on a commission legislative, executive, and judicial powers

a14-s2.title: Eight-hour day on public works
a14-s2.plain: Mechanics and workers on public works may not work more than eight hours a day, except in wartime or extraordinary emergencies that endanger life or property. The Legislature must provide for enforcement.
limits: may not exceed eight hours a day

a14-s3.title: Mechanics' and laborers' liens
a14-s3.plain: Mechanics, material suppliers, artisans and laborers have a lien on the property they worked on or supplied, for the value of the labor and material. The Legislature must provide by law for speedy and efficient enforcement of these liens.
rights: shall have a lien upon the property upon which they have bestowed labor or furnished material

a14-s4.title: Workers' compensation system
a14-s4.plain: The Legislature has plenary power, unlimited by any provision of this Constitution, to create and enforce a complete system of workers' compensation, regardless of fault, and to provide how disputes are settled, subject to review by the appellate courts.
powers: is hereby expressly vested with plenary power, unlimited by any provision of this Constitution, to create, and enforce a complete system of workers’ compensation
to create and enforce a liability on the part of any or all persons to compensate any or all of their workers
is vested with plenary powers, to provide for the settlement of any disputes arising under such legislation
may fix and control the method and manner of trial of any such dispute
may combine in one statute all the provisions for a complete system of workers’ compensation
shall have power to provide for the payment of an award to the State

a14-s5.title: Contracts for inmate labor programs
a14-s5.plain: The Director of Corrections, a county sheriff or other jail official may contract with public entities and organizations for programs that use inmate labor, but not with an employer to replace striking or locked-out workers. This section creates no right of inmates to work.
powers: may enter into contracts with public entities, nonprofit or for profit organizations, entities, or businesses for the purpose of conducting programs which use inmate labor
limits: No contract shall be executed with an employer that will initiate employment by inmates in the same job classification as non-inmate employees of the same employer who are on strike
shall not exceed, for the duration of the strike, the average daily hours worked for the preceding six months

a15-s1.title: Interest rates and usury
a15-s1.plain: Sets the legal interest rate at 7 percent a year, but parties may contract in writing for up to 10 percent on personal loans, or a market-based rate on others. Fees may not exceed the authorized interest. Listed lenders are exempt. Judgment interest is capped at 10 percent.
rights: it shall be competent for the parties to any loan or forbearance of any money, goods or things in action to contract in writing for a rate of interest
powers: The Legislature may from time to time prescribe the maximum rate per annum of, or provide for the supervision, or the filing of a schedule of, or in any manner fix, regulate or limit, the fees
limits: at a rate not exceeding 10 percent per annum
at a rate not exceeding the higher of (a) 10 percent per annum or (b) 5 percent per annum plus the rate prevailing

No person, association, copartnership or corporation shall by charging any fee, bonus, commission, discount or other compensation receive from a borrower more than the interest authorized by this section
at not more than 10 percent per annum

a16-s1.title: Limit on state debt
a16-s1.plain: The Legislature may not create debts over $300,000, except for war, unless a law for a single specified object provides for repayment within 50 years, passes by two-thirds of each house, and is approved by a majority of voters. The Legislature may raise interest rates on unsold bonds.
powers: may, at any time after the approval of such law by the people, reduce the amount of the indebtedness authorized by the law
may repeal the law if no debt shall have been contracted in pursuance thereof
may raise the maximum rate of interest payable on all general obligation bonds authorized but not sold
limits: shall not, in any manner create any debt or debts, liability or liabilities
no such law shall take effect unless it has been passed by a two-thirds vote of all the members elected to each house of the Legislature
shall be applied only to the specific object therein stated or to the payment of the debt thereby created

a16-s1.3.title: Borrowing for the accumulated budget deficit
a16-s1.3.plain: Funding the accumulated state budget deficit, as authorized by the March 2, 2004 measure, counts as a single object or work under Section 1. After those bonds issue, the State may not borrow in the listed ways to fund a year-end budget deficit.
limits: the State may not obtain moneys to fund a year-end state budget deficit

a16-s1.5.title: General Obligation Bond Proceeds Fund
a16-s1.5.plain: The Legislature may create a General Obligation Bond Proceeds Fund in the State Treasury and route bond proceeds into it, with a separate account for each bond issue paid out only as its bond law allows. It may abolish and later re-establish separate bond proceeds funds.
powers: may create and establish a “General Obligation Bond Proceeds Fund” in the State Treasury
may provide for the proceeds of the sale of general obligation bonds of the State
may abolish, subject to the conditions of this section, any fund in the State Treasury
re-establishing any bond proceeds fund so abolished
limits: shall be paid out only in accordance with the law authorizing the issuance of the particular bonds from which the proceeds were derived

a16-s2.title: State bonds by statute, not constitutional amendment
a16-s2.plain: No constitutional amendment providing for state bonds may be submitted to the voters or take effect; bond measures must be submitted as a bond act or statute. Listed bond sections of Article XVI are repealed and continued as statutes the Legislature may later amend or repeal.
powers: may amend or repeal such provisions when the bonds issued thereunder have been fully retired
limits: No amendment to this Constitution which provides for the preparation, issuance and sale of bonds of the State of California shall hereafter be submitted to the electors

a16-s3.title: No state money for private institutions, with exceptions
a16-s3.plain: No state money or property may go to any institution not under the State's exclusive management and control, except that the Legislature may fund certain hospital construction and aid institutions for orphans and the aged, and needy blind and physically handicapped persons.
powers: nothing in this Constitution shall prevent the Legislature from making state money available for that purpose
shall have the power to grant aid to the institutions conducted for the support and maintenance of minor orphans
shall have the power to grant aid to needy blind persons
shall have power to grant aid to needy physically handicapped persons
shall have at any time the right to inquire into the management of such institutions
limits: No money shall ever be appropriated or drawn from the State Treasury
nor shall any grant or donation of property ever be made thereto by the State
no person concerned with the administration of aid to needy blind persons shall dictate how any applicant or recipient shall expend such aid granted him

a16-s3.5.title: Protection of the Medi-Cal hospital fee act
a16-s3.5.plain: Statutes amending the Medi-Cal Hospital Reimbursement Improvement Act of 2013 need voter approval, except that the Legislature may, by a two-thirds vote, amend it to further its purposes or repeal it entirely. Fee proceeds are not counted as revenues for school funding and spending limits.
powers: amend or add provisions that further the purposes of the act
Nothing in this section shall prohibit the Legislature from repealing the act in its entirety
limits: No statute amending or adding to the provisions of the Medi-Cal Hospital Reimbursement Improvement Act of 2013 shall become effective
the Legislature shall not be permitted to repeal the act and replace it with a similar statute imposing a tax, fee, or assessment

a16-s4.title: Loan guarantees for hospital construction
a16-s4.plain: The Legislature may insure or guarantee loans to nonprofit corporations and public agencies for building, expanding or repairing public or nonprofit hospitals and related facilities. No provision of the Constitution limits this authority.
powers: shall have the power to insure or guarantee loans made by private or public lenders to nonprofit corporations and public agencies

a16-s5.title: No public money for religious purposes
a16-s5.plain: Neither the Legislature nor any local government may appropriate, pay or grant anything to aid any religious sect, church, creed or sectarian purpose, or support any institution controlled by one. Aid under Section 3 of Article XVI is still allowed.
limits: shall ever make an appropriation, or pay from any public fund whatever, or grant anything to or in aid of any religious sect, church, creed, or sectarian purpose
nor shall any grant or donation of personal property or real estate ever be made by the State

a16-s6.title: No gift or loan of public credit or money
a16-s6.plain: The Legislature may not give or lend public credit, make gifts of public money, or let the State or local bodies buy corporate stock. Exceptions cover irrigation district stock, local insurance pools, aid to war veterans, disaster debris clearing, and temporary treasurer transfers.
powers: may in the manner authorized by law, acquire the stock of any foreign corporation
may acquire and hold the stock of corporations, domestic or foreign
the treasurer of any city, county, or city and county shall have power
limits: shall have no power to give or to lend, or to authorize the giving or lending, of the credit of the State
nor shall it have power to make any gift or authorize the making of any gift, of any public money or thing of value
it shall not have power to authorize the State, or any political subdivision thereof, to subscribe for stock
shall not exceed 85 percent of the anticipated revenues accruing to such political subdivision

a16-s7.title: Money drawn only by appropriation and warrant
a16-s7.plain: Money may be drawn from the Treasury only through an appropriation made by law and upon a warrant duly drawn by the Controller.
limits: Money may be drawn from the Treasury only through an appropriation made by law

a16-s8.title: Minimum state funding for schools
a16-s8.plain: State revenues must first set apart money for public schools and higher education. From 1990–91, state support for school and community college districts must be at least the greatest of the listed amounts, with a maintenance factor in some years.
powers: may be suspended for one year by the enactment of an urgency statute pursuant to Section 8 of Article IV
limits: the urgency statute may not be made part of or included within any bill enacted pursuant to Section 12 of Article IV

a16-s8.5.title: Extra revenues transferred to the State School Fund
a16-s8.5.plain: The Controller must each year transfer revenues available under Article XIII B to the State School Fund, by enrollment, unless spending and class size reach the listed levels. The money is for instructional improvement and accountability; school districts must prepare audits and School Accountability Report Cards.
limits: shall be expended solely for the purposes of instructional improvement and accountability

a16-s9.title: Fish and game money
a16-s9.plain: Money collected under any state law relating to the protection or propagation of fish and game must be used for activities relating to fish and game.
limits: shall be used for activities relating thereto

a16-s10.title: State cooperation in federal aid for the aged
a16-s10.plain: When the United States provides pensions or other aid for the aged, the State may cooperate as provided by law. Local money spent under this section is not counted in the base for the spending limit under Section 20 of Article XI.
powers: co-operation by the State therewith and therein is hereby authorized

a16-s11.title: Legislative power over relief of hardship
a16-s11.plain: The Legislature has plenary power to provide for administering relief and may reshape the powers of relief agencies. The Legislature, or the people by initiative, may amend or repeal relief laws, administer relief directly or through counties, and aid or reimburse the counties.
powers: has plenary power to provide for the administration of any constitutional provisions or laws
may modify, transfer, or enlarge the powers vested in any state agency or officer
shall have power to amend, alter, or repeal any law relating to the relief of hardship and destitution

a16-s13.title: Release of liens for aid to the aged
a16-s13.plain: The Legislature may release, cancel or nullify, in whole or in part, any lien, obligation or other security it imposed to secure repayment to the State or counties of aid lawfully granted to aged persons.
powers: shall have power to release, rescind, cancel, or otherwise nullify in whole or in part any encumbrance on property

a16-s14.title: Revenue bonds for pollution control facilities
a16-s14.plain: The Legislature may provide for revenue bonds to finance pollution control facilities and their lease or sale. The bonds may not be secured by the State's taxing power, and either house may block or limit an issue by resolution.
powers: may provide for the issuance of revenue bonds to finance the acquisition, construction, and installation of environmental pollution control facilities
may, by resolution adopted by either house, prohibit or limit any proposed issuance of such revenue bonds
limits: such revenue bonds shall not be secured by the taxing power of the State
Nothing herein contained shall authorize any public agency to operate any industrial or commercial enterprise

a16-s14.5.title: Revenue bonds for alternative energy facilities
a16-s14.5.plain: The Legislature may provide for revenue bonds to finance cogeneration, solar, biomass or other alternative energy facilities and their lease or sale. The bonds may not be secured by the State's taxing power, and both houses may block or limit an issue.
powers: may provide for the issuance of revenue bonds to finance the acquisition, construction, and installation of facilities utilizing cogeneration technology, solar power, biomass, or any other alternative source
may, by resolution adopted by both houses, prohibit or limit any proposed issuance of such revenue bonds
limits: such revenue bonds shall not be secured by the taxing power of the State
Nothing contained herein shall authorize any public agency to operate any industrial or commercial enterprise

a16-s15.title: Parking meter revenue as security for parking bonds
a16-s15.plain: A public body authorized to issue securities for public parking facilities, and any other public body whose area includes those facilities, may make street parking meter revenues available as additional security.
powers: are authorized to make revenues from street parking meters available as additional security

a16-s16.title: Tax increment financing for redevelopment
a16-s16.plain: Redevelopment project property is taxed like other property. The Legislature may let a redevelopment plan divide those taxes: the base amount goes to the taxing agencies and the increase to the redevelopment agency to repay its debts, and may be pledged.
powers: The Legislature may provide that any redevelopment plan may contain a provision
The Legislature may also provide that in any redevelopment plan

a16-s17.title: State stock limits and public pension board authority
a16-s17.plain: The State may not loan its credit or hold corporate stock, except mutual water company stock held to supply water. Public pension retirement boards have plenary authority and fiduciary responsibility over investments and administration, and must act solely for participants and beneficiaries.
powers: is hereby authorized to acquire and hold shares of the capital stock of any mutual water company or corporation
shall have plenary authority
shall have the sole and exclusive power to provide for actuarial services
may by statute continue to prohibit certain investments by a retirement board
limits: The State shall not in any manner loan its credit
shall not be changed, amended, or modified by the Legislature

a16-s18.title: Local debt limit and school bond votes
a16-s18.plain: Local governments and school bodies may not incur debt beyond a year's income without two-thirds voter approval and a tax to repay it, except that bonds to fix unsafe school buildings need a majority, and certain school facility bonds need 55 percent. Each proposition is counted separately.
limits: shall incur any indebtedness or liability in any manner or for any purpose exceeding in any year the income and revenue provided for such year

a16-s19.title: Special assessment limits for charter cities and counties
a16-s19.plain: Charter cities and counties paying for public improvements or acquisitions by special assessment must follow the laws on cost limits, valuation, excess costs and majority protest, unless the legislative body, after notice and hearing, finds by a four-fifths vote that public convenience and necessity require the work.
limits: shall be undertaken only in accordance with the provisions of law governing

a16-s20.title: Budget Stabilization Account
a16-s20.plain: Creates the Budget Stabilization Account. The Controller must transfer 1.5 percent of General Fund revenues, plus certain capital gains revenues, to it each year, with half used through 2029–30 for listed debts. The balance is capped at 10 percent of tax proceeds.
powers: the Legislature may appropriate up to 50 percent
may utilize funds in the Budget Stabilization Account
limits: shall not exceed an amount that would result in a balance in the account that, when the transfer is made, exceeds 10 percent
may be expended only for infrastructure
shall not interfere with the purposes of the Budget Stabilization Account

a16-s21.title: Public School System Stabilization Account
a16-s21.plain: Creates the Public School System Stabilization Account. The Controller must transfer certain General Fund amounts to it each year, subject to listed limits, and the State must appropriate money from it for school districts and community college districts when funding falls short.
powers: may utilize funds in the Public School System Stabilization Account
limits: no amount shall be transferred to the Public School System Stabilization Account pursuant to subdivision (b) for a fiscal year for which a maintenance factor is determined
No transfer shall be made for a year for which it was determined, based on the Budget Act for that fiscal year, that this condition would not be met
no amount shall be transferred to the Public School System Stabilization Account for any fiscal year for which any of the provisions of subdivision (b) of Section 8 are suspended
shall not exceed an amount that would result in a balance in the account that is in excess of 10 percent
shall not interfere with the purposes of the Public School System Stabilization Account

a16-s22.title: Budget emergencies and reserve withdrawals
a16-s22.plain: After the Governor proclaims a budget emergency, the Legislature may pass a bill suspending or reducing transfers to the Budget Stabilization Account or the Public School System Stabilization Account, or using their funds. The section defines "budget emergency" and limits how much may be withdrawn.
powers: the Legislature may pass a bill that does any of the following
limits: Not more than 50 percent of the balance in the Budget Stabilization Account may be returned to the General Fund
shall not exceed either an amount that would result in a total General Fund expenditure level for a fiscal year that is greater than the highest amount of total General Fund expenditures

a16-s23.title: Tobacco tax revenue excluded from school funding base
a16-s23.plain: The tax imposed by the California Healthcare, Research and Prevention Tobacco Tax Act of 2016, and its revenue, are not considered General Fund revenues, state revenues, or General Fund proceeds of taxes for purposes of Section 8 and its implementing statutes.

a18-s1.title: Legislature may propose amendments or revision
a18-s1.plain: By a two-thirds rollcall vote of each house, the Legislature may propose an amendment or revision of the Constitution, and in the same manner amend or withdraw its proposal. Each amendment must be prepared and submitted so it can be voted on separately.
powers: may propose an amendment or revision of the Constitution
may amend or withdraw its proposal

a18-s2.title: Constitutional convention
a18-s2.plain: By a two-thirds rollcall vote of each house, the Legislature may ask voters at a general election whether to call a convention to revise the Constitution. If the majority vote yes, the Legislature must provide for the convention within 6 months; delegates are voters elected from districts.
powers: may submit at a general election the question whether to call a convention to revise the Constitution

a18-s3.title: Amendment by initiative
a18-s3.plain: The electors may amend the Constitution by initiative.
powers: may amend the Constitution by initiative

a18-s4.title: Voter approval and effective date of amendments
a18-s4.plain: A proposed amendment or revision must be submitted to the electors. If a majority approve, it takes effect on the fifth day after the Secretary of State files the statement of the vote, unless it provides a later operative date. Among conflicting measures, the one with most affirmative votes prevails.

a19-s1.title: No borrowing from the Highway Users Tax Account
a19-s1.plain: The Legislature may not borrow revenue from the Highway Users Tax Account, or its successor, or use these revenues for purposes or in ways other than those specifically permitted by this article.
limits: shall not borrow revenue from the Highway Users Tax Account
shall not use these revenues for purposes, or in ways, other than those specifically permitted by this article

a19-s2.title: Uses of motor vehicle fuel tax revenues
a19-s2.plain: State motor vehicle fuel tax revenues, after collection costs and refunds, go into the Highway Users Tax Account, a trust fund, are allocated monthly under Section 4, and may be used solely for public streets and highways and for exclusive public mass transit guideways.
limits: shall be used solely for the following purposes

a19-s3.title: Uses of vehicle fee and tax revenues
a19-s3.plain: State revenues from fees and taxes on vehicles or their use or operation, after collection costs and refunds, are to be used for state administration and enforcement of vehicle laws and related emissions mitigation, and for the purposes in Section 2.

a19-s4.title: Allocation of highway revenues to local areas
a19-s4.plain: The statutory formulas in effect on June 30, 2009, for allocating fuel tax revenues to cities, counties and areas stay in effect. The Legislature may change them only after set findings, hearings and a report, by a two-thirds vote, and may not divert or delay these revenues.
limits: shall not modify the statutory allocations in effect on June 30, 2009
shall not modify the statutory allocation pursuant to subdivision (b)
may be used solely by the entity to which they are allocated
may not take any action which permanently or temporarily does any of the following

a19-s5.title: Local voter approval for mass transit use
a19-s5.plain: Revenues allocated under Section 4 may not be spent on mass transit guideways, except for research and planning, until approved by a majority of voters in the area where they are to be spent. The Legislature may authorize these revenues to pay voter-approved guideway bonds.
powers: may authorize the revenues approved for allocation or expenditure under this section to be pledged or used for the payment of principal and interest on voter-approved bonds
limits: may not be expended for the purposes specified in subdivision (b) of Section 2

a19-s6.title: Highway revenues pledged for bonds
a19-s6.plain: Up to 25 percent of highway revenues allocated to the State may be pledged or used, with voter approval and legislative appropriation, to pay voter-approved state highway bonds. Up to 25 percent of a city's or county's allocation may be pledged or used only by it for its voter-approved bonds.
powers: may be pledged or used by the State
may be pledged or used only by any city or county

a19-s7.title: Replacement revenue for highway taxes
a19-s7.plain: If the Legislature reduces or repeals the fuel taxes in Section 2 and adopts a replacement revenue source, the replacement revenue goes into the Highway Users Tax Account, is dedicated to Section 2 purposes and allocated under Section 4, and is subject to all of this article.

a19-s8.title: Sales tax and vehicle license fees excluded
a19-s8.plain: This article does not affect or apply to fees or taxes imposed under the Sales and Use Tax Law or the Vehicle License Fee Law, including all amendments and additions to them.

a19-s9.title: Surplus local property used for parks
a19-s9.plain: Real property bought with these designated tax revenues by an entity other than the State, and no longer required for those purposes, may be used for local public park and recreational purposes.
powers: may be used for local public park and recreational purposes

a19-s10.title: Transfer of surplus coastal property
a19-s10.plain: The Legislature may by statute authorize transferring surplus state property in the coastal zone, bought with these tax revenues, for at least its acquisition cost, to listed state park, fish and wildlife, wildlife conservation and coastal conservancy agencies for their purposes. The section defines "coastal zone."
powers: may authorize the transfer of such property

a19a-s1.title: Public Transportation Account protected
a19a-s1.plain: The Public Transportation Account is a trust fund. The Legislature may not borrow from it, change its status, or divert or delay its revenues, which may be used only for transportation planning and mass transportation and are continuously appropriated to the Controller for allocation. Key terms are defined.
limits: shall not borrow revenues from the Public Transportation Account
shall not use these revenues for purposes, or in ways, other than those specifically permitted by this article
may not change the status of the Public Transportation Account as a trust fund
may not be loaned or otherwise transferred to the General Fund or any other fund or account in the State Treasury
may not take any action which temporarily or permanently diverts or appropriates these revenues
may only be used for transportation planning and mass transportation purposes
may not take any action that temporarily or permanently diverts or appropriates these revenues

a19a-s2.title: Local transportation funds protected
a19a-s2.plain: Local transportation funds are trust funds that may not be abolished. Their money may be allocated only by the local government that created the fund and only for set purposes, and the Legislature may not divert, borrow or reduce these revenues.
limits: may not change the status of local transportation funds as trust funds
may not be abolished
shall be allocated only by the local government that created the fund
Neither the county nor the Legislature may authorize the expenditure of money in a local transportation fund for purposes other than those specified in this subdivision
may not enact a statute or take any other action which, permanently or temporarily, does any of the following
shall not be reduced below the percentage that was transmitted to such funds during the 2008 calendar year

a19b-s1.title: No borrowing from the Transportation Investment Fund
a19b-s1.plain: The Legislature may not borrow revenues from the Transportation Investment Fund, or its successor, or use these revenues for purposes or in ways other than those specifically permitted by this article.
limits: shall not borrow revenues from the Transportation Investment Fund
shall not use these revenues for purposes, or in ways, other than those specifically permitted by this article

a19b-s2.title: Motor vehicle fuel sales tax revenues for transportation
a19b-s2.plain: Sales and use tax revenues on motor vehicle fuel must be deposited into the Transportation Investment Fund, a trust fund, and used only for public transit, transportation capital projects, and city and county street and highway work, in set shares. The Legislature may not divert or borrow them.
powers: The Legislature may provide by statute for the issuance of bonds
limits: The Legislature may not change the status of the Transportation Investment Fund as a trust fund
The Legislature may not enact a statute that modifies the percentage shares set forth in subdivision (c)
The Legislature may not enact a statute or take any other action

a19c-s1.title: Restoring unlawfully diverted transportation funds
a19c-s1.plain: If a challenge to an action that violates Article XIX, XIX A, or XIX B succeeds, enough General Fund revenue is continuously appropriated to the Controller to restore the fund or account from which revenues were unlawfully taken or diverted.

a19c-s2.title: Restoring unlawfully diverted local revenues
a19c-s2.plain: If a challenge to an action that violates Section 24 or Section 25.5 of Article XIII succeeds, an amount equal to the revenue unlawfully taken or diverted is continuously appropriated from the General Fund to the local government.

a19c-s3.title: Interest and timing of restored funds
a19c-s3.plain: Interest at the Pooled Money Investment Fund rate accrues on amounts to be restored. Within 30 days after a challenge succeeds, the Controller must make the transfer and notify the parties it is complete.

a19c-s4.title: No bond required for injunctions in challenges
a19c-s4.plain: In a challenge brought under this section, if a restraining order or preliminary injunction is issued, the plaintiffs or petitioners do not have to post a bond to indemnify the government defendants or the State for any damage it may cause.
rights: the plaintiffs or petitioners shall not be required to post a bond

a19d-s1.title: Vehicle license fee revenues for transportation
a19d-s1.plain: Vehicle license fee revenues, beyond collection costs and refunds, must be used only for transportation purposes, not to pay certain state transportation bonds. Except as allowed by two Government Code sections, the Legislature may not borrow these revenues or use them otherwise.
limits: shall not be used for the payment of principal and interest on state transportation general obligation bonds
the Legislature shall not borrow the revenues described in subdivision (a)
shall not use these revenues for purposes, or in ways, other than as authorized in subdivisions (a) or (b)

a20-s1.title: Consolidation of Sacramento city and county
a20-s1.plain: The County of Sacramento and any of its cities may be consolidated by statute as a charter city and county, with approval of a majority of the county's voters on the question. The resulting City and County is both a charter city and a charter county.
powers: may be consolidated as a charter city and county as provided by statute

a20-s1.5.title: Homestead protection from forced sale
a20-s1.5.plain: The Legislature must protect by law a certain portion of the homestead and other property of all heads of families from forced sale.

a20-s2.title: Stanford University and Huntington Library
a20-s2.plain: Except for tax exemptions provided in Article XIII, the rights, powers, privileges, and confirmations given by Sections 10 and 15 of Article IX, as in effect on January 1, 1973, relating to Stanford University and the Huntington Library and Art Gallery, continue in effect.

a20-s3.title: Oath of office for public officers
a20-s3.plain: Members of the Legislature and all public officers and employees, except inferior ones exempted by law, must take the stated oath or affirmation before entering office. No other oath, declaration, or test may be required as a qualification for public office or employment.
limits: no other oath, declaration, or test, shall be required as a qualification for any public office or employment

a20-s4.title: Franchise leasing cannot avoid liabilities
